event.structure: Swiss into a single-elimination top cut, open team lists
event.seeding: seeded so the quarter-final pairings match the real bracket

briefing:
This bracket replays the top 8 of 2026 Pokémon VGC World Championship, a 395-player Pokémon Champions tournament played 28-30 August 2026 under VGC Regulation Set M-B (Swiss into a single-elimination top cut, open team lists).
Every team here, yours and your opponent’s alike, is one a player took to that top cut; nobody in this bracket built their own. Which of them placed where is not disclosed.
The published lists gave species, items, abilities, natures and moves but no stat points, so every spread here was rebuilt from public sets of the same Pokémon in this regulation and is not the players’ own.

decisions.rationale: Lead Kingambit + Whimsicott: Whimsicott is immune to Sleep Powder and gets prankster Tailwind to outspeed scarf Garchomp and Chlorophyll Venusaur, while Kingambit converts Incineroar's Intimidate into Defiant boosts and resists Dark/Sucker Punch coverage. Fire weakness is cushioned by occaberry. Back Garchomp (Rock Slide for Charizard, EQ for Venusaur/Incineroar) and Charizard-Y as the Mega/weather answer, covering the Toxapex-Incineroar stall core.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun stall core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) plus Incineroar/Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1 plan: lead Kingambit+Whimsicott, Tailwind turn 1, keep Kingambit healthy as Sucker Punch/Defiant wincon vs Charizard and Intimidate. Whimsicott immune to Sleep Powder. Only one Mega per game: my Charizard-Y. Watch Fake Out on Kingambit; occaberry covers Heat Wave chip.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar with Mega Charizard Y for immediate Intimidate/Fake Out support and sun pressure; Venusaur completes the sun mode while Sylveon checks opposing Garchomp, Kingambit, and Dark-types.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Kingambit has Defiant, so avoid low-value Intimidate triggers when it is healthy. Charizard-Y plus Venusaur is the preferred proactive mode, blunting Basculegion and pressuring Fairy-types; preserve Sylveon as the principal answer to Garchomp and Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Low Kick 2x on Incineroar with Defiant boost can OHKO (59-107%); occaberry keeps Kingambit safe from sun Heat Wave (~25-35%, halved by berry). Whimsicott gets Prankster Tailwind up; Fake Out most likely targets Kingambit, and even if Kingambit flinches Tailwind still resolves.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun stall core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) plus Incineroar/Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1: lead Kingambit+Whimsicott worked; Kingambit has net +1 Atk (Defiant) and occaberry makes foe Zard-Y Heat Wave trivial (~13-18% after berry). Low Kick 80BP is 59-107% on Incineroar (sitrus may save it). Whimsicott immune to Sleep Powder. Only one Mega per game: my Charizard-Y. Watch scarf Garchomp under my Tailwind; keep Kingambit healthy as Sucker Punch wincon.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out Kingambit guarantees a flinch (it has no Protect) and removes the possible +1 Kowtow Cleave OHKO on Charizard this turn, while Mega Charizard-Y sets Drought and Heat Wave burns Kingambit's Occa Berry and breaks Whimsicott's Focus Sash (or forces its Protect). If Whimsicott takes the free Tailwind instead, our sun-boosted Chlorophyll Venusaur pivot next turn still outspeeds Tailwinded Kingambit, and Sylveon remains the long-term answer to Kingambit/Garchomp. Avoiding Parting Shot prevents another Defiant trigger.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Kingambit has Defiant with no Protect and Occa Berry (now likely burned); avoid low-value Intimidate/Parting Shot triggers while it is healthy. Whimsicott is the Tailwind/Encore support with Focus Sash and Prankster. Charizard-Y plus Venusaur is the preferred proactive mode: Chlorophyll Venusaur (264 effective Speed in sun) outspeeds even Tailwinded Kingambit, and sun blunts Basculegion while pressuring Fairy-types; preserve Sylveon as the principal answer to Garchomp and Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Both Heat Wave (99.5-139%) and Flare Blitz (95.7-139%) are guaranteed KOs on Kingambit at 30% with the Occa Berry gone, and Sucker Punch only does 50-96% to Zard-Y (Moonblast adds just 11-20%), so staying trades Kingambit for at most a coin-flip chip. Preserving the +1 Atk Sucker Punch wincon by withdrawing is clearly better. Whimsicott at 1% is dead to any spread hit regardless, so it spends its last turn Prankster-Encoring Incineroar into Fake Out, which fails on turn 2 — denying Incineroar's action and locking it if it stays. Kingambit goes to Charizard, which resists Heat Wave (0.5x) and keeps our own Mega available to punish under our Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun stall core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) plus Incineroar/Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1 facts: foe Zard-Y Heat Wave 99.5-139% and Incineroar Flare Blitz 95.7-139% both guaranteed KO on Kingambit below ~40% without Occa Berry (consumed turn 1). My +1 Sucker Punch = 50-96% on foe Zard-Y (not a KO); Whimsicott Moonblast vs Zard-Y only 11-20%; Low Kick 59-107% on Incineroar (Sitrus likely saves). Incineroar Fake Out now spent, immune to Encore lock into Fake Out. Only one Mega per game: mine is Charizard-Y. Whimsicott immune to Sleep Powder; beware Venusaur under sun (Chlorophyll) and scarf Garchomp under my Tailwind. Plan: keep Kingambit healthy as the Sucker Punch late-game wincon; Tailwind is the tempo edge — leverage my own Zard-Y Mega + Drought next, Whimsicott is nearly dead so treat it as expendable for Encore/tempo.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit at +1 can OHKO Charizard with Kowtow Cleave (81-115%) and may outspeed under Tailwind, so Charizard Protects; Protect's +4 priority also makes Whimsicott's Prankster Encore fail against it. Incineroar's Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on Kingambit at 29% through any spread, removing the Defiant threat. Worst case Whimsicott Encores Incineroar into Flare Blitz, which I can clear by switching to Venusaur next turn; Whimsicott sits at 1% and dies to any hit afterward while Tailwind ticks down.

Mega Evolve to refresh Drought and keep Tailwind Speed advantage, hit foe Zard-Y's 4x weakness with Ancient Power (near-KO range after Mega's SpA jump, survives their Heat Wave even on high rolls), and Prankster-Encore Zard-Y into repeating its reduced-accuracy Protect, wasting their Mega's turns while Whimsicott is expendable at 1%.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun stall core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) plus Incineroar/Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1 facts: foe Zard-Y Heat Wave does only 32.9-46.5% to my Zard (survivable from 55%); my Ancient Power pre-Mega 47.6-86.3% on foe Zard-Y, meaningfully higher after Mega-Y SpA boost — 4x Rock is the answer to their Zard. Kingambit facts: +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on foe Zard-Y; Low Kick 59-107% on Incineroar (Sitrus likely saves); foe Zard-Y Heat Wave and Incineroar Flare Blitz both KO Kingambit below ~40% without Occa (Occa consumed turn 1) — keep Kingambit healthy as late-game Sucker Punch wincon. Incineroar Fake Out is spent; immune to Encore lock into Fake Out. Whimsicott immune to Sleep Powder; wary of Venusaur Chlorophyll under sun and scarf Garchomp under my Tailwind. Only one Mega per game — mine is Charizard-Y, used turn 3 with Drought refreshed. Encore on a fresh Protect user locks them into repeating Protect at reduced success.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott fainted, so the replacement should be Garchomp: at 100% HP and 338 effective Speed under Tailwind it outruns Chlorophyll Venusaur (200-264), scarf Garchomp (244-308) and everything else, threatens Venusaur with Earth Power-proof coverage (my Flying Zard is immune to Earthquake, so no friendly fire), and pressures Incineroar. Kingambit at 30% without its Occa Berry is KO'd by Incineroar's Flare Blitz or foe Zard-Y Heat Wave, so it must stay benched as the late-game Sucker Punch wincon. Charizard passes this turn while the replacement enters.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar/Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1 facts: foe Zard-Y Heat Wave 32.9-46.5% on my Zard; my Ancient Power ~4x on their Zard-Y (47.6-86.3% pre-Mega, higher after Mega SpA). Kingambit: +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on foe Zard-Y; Low Kick 59-107% on Incineroar; without Occa Berry, foe Zard-Y Heat Wave and Incineroar Flare Blitz KO it below ~40% — it is the late-game wincon, keep benched until safe. Incineroar Fake Out spent turn 1; immune to Encore into Fake Out. Encore on fresh Protect locks repeated Protect. Whimsicott immune to Sleep Powder. My Tailwind and sun are short-lived; my Garchomp under Tailwind outruns Chlorophyll Venusaur and scarf Garchomp, and EQ is safe beside Flying Zard. Venusaur entered with Focus Sash intact but fell below full turn 3, so Sash is no longer a factor.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott's Prankster Encore threatens to lock Mega Charizard into a guaranteed-fail consecutive Protect while foe Charizard's 4x Ancient Power does 56.8-85.2% — a terrible trade for our primary attacker. Switching Charizard to Venusaur makes Encore fail (fresh switch-in has no prior move) and dodges Ancient Power, preserving Charizard at 100% for later (Drought resets sun on re-entry). Incineroar's Flare Blitz in sun is a guaranteed KO on the 1% Whimsicott, permanently removing the Tailwind/Encore support before it can disrupt again; even if it Protects, it remains at 1%. Venusaur enters safely behind Focus Sash with Chlorophyll speed and Sleep Powder pressure for next turn; Kingambit's Defiant punishes Parting Shot, so pivoting that way is undesirable.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Kingambit (benched, low HP) has Defiant, no Protect, Occa Berry burned — never give it free Intimidate/Parting Shot triggers. Whimsicott is Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Protect support; its Encore cannot touch Dark-type Incineroar but threatens Charizard/Venusaur/Sylveon, so pivot switch-ins to dodge it. Foe Charizard carries Ancient Power (4x vs our Charizard-Y) and is tailwind-fast. Preserve Mega Charizard-Y as the primary attacker; Drought re-triggers on its re-entry to renew sun for Chlorophyll Venusaur. Venusaur (Focus Sash, Sleep Powder) is the proactive mid-game mode; Sylveon is reserved as the main answer to Garchomp and Kingambit. Opponent's unrevealed fourth is one of Basculegion/Garchomp/Floette — sun blunts Basculegion, watch for Garchomp Earthquake or Floette Fairy damage.

decisions.rationale: Heat Wave is a guaranteed KO on Venusaur (89.8-162.6% from 70%; Sash already broken) even through spread reduction, removing the Sleep Powder threat; Garchomp's EQ can't touch my Flying Zard and lands 44.6-81.2% on Incineroar, who can't KO either of mine back (Flare Blitz resisted by both). If Venusaur Protects, EQ still massively chips Incineroar and sun's last turns keep Heat Wave lethal next turn.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar plus one hidden of Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1 facts: my Zard-Y Heat Wave KOs Venusaur from 70% guaranteed (spread-adjusted); Garchomp EQ 44.6-81.2% on Incineroar from 88% (Sitrus); Rock Slide only 22.8-41.2% on Incineroar and neutral on Venusaur, so EQ is the better Garchomp attack beside Zard. Kingambit: +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on foe Zard-Y; Low Kick 59-107% on Incineroar; without Occa Berry, foe Zard-Y Heat Wave and Incineroar Flare Blitz KO it below ~40% — keep benched until safe. Incineroar Fake Out spent turn 1; immune to Encore into Fake Out. Encore on fresh Protect locks repeated Protect. Whimsicott fainted turn 3. My Garchomp under Tailwind outruns Chlorophyll Venusaur and scarf Garchomp; EQ is safe beside Flying Zard. Venusaur's Focus Sash broken (fell below full turn 3).

decisions.rationale: Both foes outspeed both our actives under Tailwind (Garchomp 268+ and foe Zard 264+ vs Venusaur 264, Incineroar 80), and their spread moves (Earthquake/Rock Slide/Heat Wave) threaten heavy damage to both our slots while Venusaur's Sash is already voided at 70%. Double Protect is safe (neither has protected yet, no failure chance), burns the last Tailwind turn, and preserves the board. Next turn Tailwind is gone and Venusaur's Chlorophyll 264 Speed outruns everything on their side, letting us Sleep Powder Garchomp or Sludge Bomb their weakened Zard while Incineroar provides Parting Shot pivoting. Attacking this turn loses Venusaur before it moves; pivoting into Charizard risks a 4x Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's full Game 1 team is now known: Kingambit (29%, Defiant, Occa Berry consumed), Whimsicott (fainted), Charizard-Mega-Y (54%, Ancient Power carrier), Garchomp (Sitrus Berry, Rough Skin, Jolly, Rock Slide/EQ/Dragon Claw/Protect). Basculegion and Floette were not brought. Never give Kingambit free Defiant triggers via Intimidate or Parting Shot (net +1 Atk for it). Foe Zard's Ancient Power is 4x vs our Charizard-Y; Garchomp's Rock Slide is also 4x vs our Charizard-Y — only bring Charizard in when Garchomp is asleep, KOed, or their Zard is gone. Core plan: once opposing Tailwind is down, Chlorophyll Venusaur (264 Spe) is the fastest thing on the field — use Sleep Powder on Garchomp or Sludge Bomb/Earth Power as appropriate; Drought re-triggers when Charizard re-enters to refresh sun. Preserve Mega Charizard-Y as the primary late-game attacker; Sylveon remains the dedicated answer to Garchomp and Kingambit (Hyper Voice, resists Dark). Incineroar's role is Fake Out plus Parting Shot pivots into safe switch-ins.

decisions.rationale: Heat Wave guarantees the KO on Venusaur (70%, Sash broken) and EQ only hits Incineroar since Charizard is Flying-immune, landing 44.6-81.2% to leave Incineroar on Sitrus range at best. Removing the 200-264 Speed Chlorophyll Venusaur before it acts (Sludge/Earth Power/Sleep Powder) is worth the risk of Incineroar's sun-boosted Flare Blitz into 55% Zard; even if Zard falls, the trade is Zard for Venusaur plus heavy chip, and the sun (and Venusaur's speed) dies this turn regardless.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar plus one hidden of Toxapex/scarf Garchomp/Sylveon. Game 1 facts: Zard-Y Heat Wave KOs Venusaur from 70% guaranteed spread-adjusted; Garchomp EQ hits only the foe beside Flying Zard-Y, 44.6-81.2% on Incineroar (Sitrus may save it); Rock Slide only 22.8-41.2% on Incineroar, neutral on Venusaur. Kingambit: +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on foe Zard-Y; Low Kick 59-107% on Incineroar; without Occa Berry, foe Zard-Y Heat Wave and Incineroar Flare Blitz KO it below ~40% — keep benched until safe. Incineroar Fake Out spent; immune to Encore into Fake Out; its Protect success is reduced from consecutive uses. Encore on fresh Protect locks repeated Protect. Whimsicott fainted turn 3. Venusaur's Focus Sash broken; its Sludge Bomb is only ~50-70% on my Zard-Y, Earth Power ~45-65% neutral on my Garchomp. My Garchomp 169 Speed outspeeds scarf Garchomp (122-154) without Tailwind; Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds everyone while sun lasts. Plan: after Venusaur is gone, finish Incineroar, then Kingambit +1 win-cons against the hidden mon (likely Toxapex/Sylveon wall — keep EQ/dark coverage in mind).

decisions.rationale: Venusaur at 264 Speed is the fastest Pokémon on the field this final sun turn. Their Charizard's Heat Wave is a guaranteed KO on Venusaur from 70%, so neutralizing it is mandatory: Sleep Powder into Charizard both protects Venusaur (Garchomp's Rock Slide maxes at ~29% into it) and removes their only real threat to my Charizard-Y; if they switch Kingambit into that slot it gets slept with no Defiant trigger. Incineroar contributes little damage here (Flare Blitz resisted by both), so Parting Shot on Garchomp chips its Attack, resets Fake Out for later, and pivots in Sylveon, my dedicated Garchomp/Kingambit answer (immune to Dragon Claw, resists Dark, Pixilate Hyper Voice is 2x SE into Garchomp). Next turn I can sleep Garchomp as well and position Charizard-Y to re-trigger Drought once Rock Slide/Ancient Power threats are neutralized.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's full Game 1 team is known: Kingambit (Defiant, Occa Berry consumed, low HP), Whimsicott (fainted), Charizard-Mega-Y (Ancient Power carrier, ~half HP), Garchomp (Sitrus Berry, Rough Skin, Jolly, Rock Slide/EQ/Dragon Claw/Protect). Basculegion and Floette were not brought. Never give Kingambit free Defiant triggers via Intimidate or Parting Shot. Foe Zard's Ancient Power and Garchomp's Rock Slide are both 4x vs our Charizard-Y — only bring Charizard in when Garchomp is asleep/KOed or their Zard is gone. Sleep Powder (75%) is the key tool: sleeping a switch-in on the targeted slot works and avoids Defiant. Incineroar's role: Fake Out (reset by pivoting) plus Parting Shot pivots. Sylveon is the answer to Garchomp (Hyper Voice 2x SE, Dragon immunity) and Kingambit (resists Dark; beware +2 Iron Head). Endgame plan: put foes to sleep, then bring Mega Charizard-Y in safely to re-trigger Drought and sweep with Heat Wave/Solar Beam. Venusaur's Focus Sash is moot once below full HP.

decisions.rationale: Sylveon is the safe pivot: it resists or survives the opposing attacks, threatens Garchomp with Pixilate Hyper Voice, and keeps Charizard-Mega-Y preserved until Garchomp or the opposing Charizard is removed.

Bringing Charizard-Mega-Y into an active Garchomp (Rock Slide) plus opposing Charizard-Y (Ancient Power) is suicidal — both carry 4x coverage. Incineroar is the correct pivot: Intimidate further neuters Garchomp (already at -1), and Fake Out can pin Garchomp in place next turn so Sylveon's Hyper Voice (2x SE) can claim the KO while chip-damaging the enemy Charizard. Once Garchomp is down, Charizard-Y can come in safely later to reset Drought for the endgame. Sylveon resists Heat Wave poorly? No — Fairy is neutral to Fire, and at full HP with 150 SpD it tanks it easily, while Incineroar resists Fire outright.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's full Game 1 team is known: Kingambit (Defiant, Occa Berry consumed, low HP, benched), Whimsicott (fainted), Charizard-Mega-Y (Ancient Power carrier, ~half HP), Garchomp (Sitrus Berry, Rough Skin, Jolly, Rock Slide/EQ/Dragon Claw/Protect). Basculegion and Floette were not brought. Never give Kingambit free Defiant triggers via Intimidate or Parting Shot. Foe Zard's Ancient Power and Garchomp's Rock Slide are both 4x vs our Charizard-Y — only bring Charizard in when Garchomp is asleep/KOed or their Zard is gone. Incineroar's role: Fake Out disruption (reset by pivoting) plus Parting Shot pivots; its Sitrus is consumed and it is low, so it is expendable chip/utility. Sylveon is the answer to Garchomp (Pixilate Hyper Voice 2x SE, Dragon immunity, Quick Attack priority Fairy chip) and walls Kingambit's Dark STAB (beware +2 Iron Head). Endgame plan: remove Garchomp via Fake Out + Hyper Voice pressure, then bring Mega Charizard-Y in safely to re-trigger Drought and sweep with Heat Wave/Solar Beam; Weather Ball becomes 100 BP Fire in sun. Venusaur is gone; Sleep Powder is no longer available, so KO paths now run through Sylveon and Charizard.

decisions.rationale: Ancient Power guarantees the KO on 26% Incineroar (33.7-61.2% into 2x weakness), removing Parting Shot/Flare Blitz before it can pivot Zard-Y in; if Incineroar Parting Shots instead, the 4x Rock hit redirects into foe Zard-Y for massive damage. Garchomp Protects: Sylveon's Hyper Voice is 71.8-107.7% on Garchomp (potential OHKO through Sitrus) but only 18.7-27.7% on Zard-Y, so protecting blanks it, blocks a Yawn, and preserves Garchomp; its offense is spent (-2 EQ is only 15-29% on Sylveon).
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon. Game 1 facts: foe brought only Incineroar, Zard-Y, Venusaur (fainted turn 5), Sylveon — no hidden 4th remains. Zard-Y Heat Wave KOs Venusaur; Garchomp EQ 44.6-81.2% on fresh Incineroar; Rock Slide weak on Incineroar. Kingambit: +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on foe Zard-Y; Low Kick 59-107% on Incineroar; without Occa Berry, foe Zard-Y Heat Wave and Incineroar Flare Blitz KO it below ~40% HP — it sits at 30% with Occa consumed, keep benched until safe. My Zard-Y Ancient Power guaranteed KO on 26% Incineroar (33.7-61.2% into 2x); Ancient Power is 4x into foe Zard-Y and redirects onto it if Incineroar Parting Shots. Sylveon (Pixilate, Fairy Feather, Quiet): Hyper Voice 71.8-107.7% on my Garchomp (Sitrus only saves below ~96% rolls), 18.7-27.7% on my Zard-Y; its Yawn/Detect exist, Hyper Voice is its main damage. My Garchomp at -2 Atk: EQ only 15.3-28.8% on Sylveon, Dragon Claw immune vs Sylveon — Garchomp is a Protect/bait body only; 169 Speed outspeeds Sylveon (72-100) and Incineroar (80-112). Kingambit's answer to Sylveon is Iron Head (Steel 2x vs Fairy); Sucker Punch only if Sylveon attacks. Plan: remove Incineroar, then handle Sylveon with Kingambit Iron Head while preserving Zard-Y as secondary; beware foe Zard-Y entry sun enabling SolarBeam (2x) on Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is the principal threat (Rock Slide 4x my Charizard) but is neutered at -2 Atk and walled by Sylveon (Dragon immunity; its EQ does only 17-24% to Sylveon). Incineroar at 27% is guaranteed dead to foe Charizard's Ancient Power if targeted, so its best use is a final Fake Out into Garchomp: flinch denies Garchomp's action and the 7-12% chip pushes Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice (67-119%) into a likely KO range on Garchomp this turn; if it barely survives, Quick Attack (Fairy 2x, priority) finishes it next turn. Sylveon is safe this turn (worst case Heat Wave ~52%, Garchomp flinched). Hyper Voice also chips foe Charizard. Trading expendable Incineroar for Garchomp's removal opens the endgame for my healthy Mega Charizard-Y once foe Charizard/Garchomp Rock coverage is gone.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Foe Zard-Y is the only real threat left: its sun Heat Wave KOs my 30% Zard-Y even resisted (~44-59% of max) and Sylveon Hyper Voice KOs my Garchomp (71.8-107.7%). Both my attackers are faster than foe Zard-Y (Garchomp 169 > my Zard-Y 167 > foe 132-167), so stacking Rock Slide (68-90% at -2 Atk, 4x) and Ancient Power (83-98%, 4x) on it removes it before it moves in the large majority of lines. If it drops, Garchomp trades to Hyper Voice and Kingambit comes in on Sylveon, which it hard-walls (Hyper Voice/Quick Attack 0.25x) while Iron Head hits 78-152% - a clean endgame with my Zard-Y still up. Even if foe Zard-Y survives on a low-roll double, Kingambit's +1 Sucker Punch cleans its remaining ~10-30% next turn. Protecting Zard-Y instead leaves a full-power Zard-Y alive with a much worse endgame.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon. Game 1: foe brought only Incineroar, Zard-Y, Venusaur (fainted), Sylveon - no hidden 4th. Incineroar fainted turn 6. Foe Zard-Y (Timid, CharizarditeY, speed 132-167) Heat Wave in sun KOs my 30% Zard-Y even resisted; Sylveon (Pixilate, Fairy Feather, Quiet, speed 72-100) Hyper Voice 71.8-107.7% on my Garchomp, only 18.7-27.7% on my Zard-Y (survives at 30%). Kingambit: at 30% HP with Occa consumed, net +1 Atk (Defiant offset Intimidate); +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on fresh foe Zard-Y; Iron Head 78-152% on Sylveon (possible but not guaranteed OHKO); Sylveon's Fairy Hyper Voice/Quick Attack are only 0.25x into Kingambit - it hard-walls Sylveon and wins the 1v1 even at low HP, but beware Sylveon Yawn sleep. My Garchomp -2 Atk: Rock Slide 68-90% on foe Zard-Y (4x, 90% acc), EQ only chips Sylveon, Dragon Claw immune vs Sylveon. My Zard-Y Ancient Power ~83-98% on fresh foe Zard-Y (4x), Heat Wave 34-59% on Sylveon. Plan vs endgame: collapse damage onto foe Zard-Y first (both attackers outspeed it), accept Garchomp trading to Hyper Voice, bring Kingambit in on Sylveon; Sucker Punch only works if target attacks, so guard against Protect stalls, and finish Sylveon with Iron Head + Zard-Y Heat Wave chip.

decisions.rationale: Our Charizard-Y is 4x weak to both foe Zard's Ancient Power (near-certain KO on our 155 HP) and Garchomp's Rock Slide, and could lose a speed tie to foe Zard, so it Protects. Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice is the key press: 67-119% into Garchomp (possible OHKO; Sitrus heal still leaves it in Quick Attack + Solar Beam KO range next turn) while also chipping the 30% foe Zard, possibly finishing it. Next turn we clean up with priority Fairy Quick Attack and Solar Beam under our sun.

Focus everything on foe Zard-Y: it's the only real damage threat left (sun Heat Wave KOs my 30% Zard-Y, and its Hyper Voice partner is walled by Kingambit). Garchomp (169 Spe) moves first with Rock Slide (68-90% on 4x), then my Zard-Y's Ancient Power (~83-98%) guarantees the KO before foe Zard-Y can act, unless it Protects (rate already reduced) or both miss. Even in the bad speed-tie line where foe Zard-Y Heat Waves first and takes my Zard-Y down, Rock Slide leaves it in KO range for Kingambit's +1 Sucker Punch, and Sylveon cannot break Kingambit (0.25x Hyper Voice).
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon. Game 1: foe brought only Incineroar, Zard-Y, Venusaur, Sylveon - no hidden 4th. Incineroar fainted t6, Venusaur fainted t5. Foe Zard-Y (Timid, CharizarditeY, 132-167 Spe): Protect rate reduced after t7 use; sun Heat Wave KOs my Zard-Y even resisted. Sylveon (Pixilate, Fairy Feather, Quiet, 72-100 Spe): Hyper Voice 71.8-107.7% on full Garchomp, only 18.7-27.7% on my Zard-Y; hard-walled by Kingambit (0.25x), beware Yawn sleep. Kingambit benched at 30%, Occa consumed, net +1 Atk: +1 Sucker Punch 50-96% on fresh foe Zard-Y (only if target attacks), Iron Head 78-152% on Sylveon. My Garchomp -2 Atk: Rock Slide 68-90% on foe Zard-Y. My Zard-Y (167 Spe): Ancient Power 83-98% on foe Zard-Y. Endgame plan: KO foe Zard-Y first with combined Rock Slide + Ancient Power (both mine move before it unless speed tie lost); then trade Garchomp to Sylveon chip if needed; bring Kingambit in to wall Sylveon and close with Sucker Punch (guard Protect stalls) or Iron Head + Zard-Y Heat Wave chip.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Yawn Garchomp to neutralize the biggest long-term threat while Charizard attempts a reduced-chance Protect against the likely Ancient Power + Rock Slide focus. Keeping Charizard alive preserves the sun endgame, and Garchomp becoming drowsy creates a safer window to attack next turn.

Sylveon is the opponent's last Pokémon. Zard-Y (167) and Garchomp (169) both outspeed its 72-100 range. Sun Weather Ball does 49.5-82.9% and Garchomp Rock Slide adds 10.4-20% for a combined 59.9-102.9% — the best shot to end the game this turn before Yawn sleeps Garchomp at turn's end. Note Hyper Voice is actually 1x on Kingambit (36-52.7%), so it would KO my 30% Kingambit; no safe switch exists. If Sylveon Detects or survives on a roll, Zard-Y (immune to being KO'd quickly, 18.7-27.7% chip) plus Kingambit can still close it out.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon. Game 1: foe brought only Incineroar, Zard-Y, Venusaur, Sylveon. All foe mons except Sylveon fainted by t9. KEY CORRECTION: Sylveon Hyper Voice is 1x on Kingambit (Fairy 2x into Dark, 0.5x into Steel), NOT 0.25x — it does 36.2-52.7% and OHKOs a 30% Kingambit; Kingambit cannot safely switch in while Sylveon lives. Damage anchors: my Zard-Y sun Weather Ball 49.5-82.9% on Sylveon (Heat Wave 46.5-79.4%, Ancient Power lower); my -2 Atk Garchomp Rock Slide 10.4-20% on Sylveon, 68-90% on foe Zard-Y; my Zard Ancient Power 83-98% on foe Zard-Y. Sylveon Hyper Voice: 71.8-107.7% on Garchomp, 18.7-27.7% on my Zard-Y (spread-reduced when two targets; higher solo). Sylveon Quiet, Pixilate, Fairy Feather, 72-100 Spe, has Detect/Yawn/Quick Attack; beware first-use Detect and sleep fishing. Kingambit benched at 30% with +1 Atk: only deploy after Sylveon is gone. Yawn sleep happens at end of following turn and Protect does not cancel it. Endgame: double-target Sylveon with Weather Ball + Rock Slide while both outspeed; fallback is Zard-Y Weather Ball 2HKOs in a 1v1 even after eating Hyper Voice chips, avoid getting Yawned.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is drowsy from last turn's Yawn and sleeps at end of this turn. Hyper Voice threatens a possible OHKO on Garchomp (67-119% range) and chips Charizard to ~2-14%. Sylveon's bulk (150 SpD, 81% HP) should survive a sun Heat Wave plus a -2 Rock Slide, and even if Garchomp survives via Sitrus Berry it falls asleep, leaving Charizard isolated against Sylveon's Fairy STAB with Kingambit at 29% in the back. Detect would waste the chance to remove Garchomp outright.

Sylveon is the foe's last Pokémon at 2%; my Zard-Y (167 Spe) outspeeds it and Weather Ball (sun-boosted) is a guaranteed KO on a 2% target, winning the game before Sylveon can move (only Detect at +4 priority could stall, and then Garchomp still has a waking shot). Garchomp is asleep, so Protect is a no-op placeholder.
decisions.notebook: Series vs sun core (Charizard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon. Game 1 won by Zard-Y Weather Ball KO on 2% Sylveon at t10. KEY CORRECTION: Sylveon Hyper Voice is 1x on Kingambit (36.2-52.7%), not 0.25x — Kingambit cannot switch in on it safely. Damage anchors (sun): my Zard-Y Weather Ball 49.5-82.9% / Heat Wave 46.5-79.4% on Sylveon; my Zard-Y Ancient Power 83-98% on foe Zard-Y; -2 Atk Garchomp Rock Slide 68-90% on foe Zard-Y, 10.4-20% on Sylveon. Sylveon: Quiet, Pixilate, Fairy Feather, 72-100 Spe, Detect/Yawn/Quick Attack/Hyper Voice; Hyper Voice 71.8-107.7% on Garchomp; beware first-use Detect (never used in game 1) and Yawn sleep-fishing. Their Zard-Y/Venusaur/Incineroar are fragile to Ancient Power/Earthquake/Heat Wave; Incineroar Fake Out is an auto-lead threat — expect it game 2 and consider Protecting the Fake Out target or hard-switching. Kingambit is a strong endgame cleaner once Intimidate user and Sylveon are gone; Whimsicott Tailwind beats their speed tier but died t3 to Flare Blitz.

decisions.rationale: Hyper Voice is a guaranteed KO on both active foes, forcing Kingambit in alone and preserving Sylveon's best chance to finish with Hyper Voice.

reflections.summary: Won 10-0 on decisions in a clean lane. The engine was Ancient Power spread pressure on my Zard-Y: it chipped Venusaur, KO'd Incineroar through Sitrus (t6), and KO'd their Zard-Y (t8) the moment their Protect failed to a double-use, all while Garchomp's Rock Slide spread softened Sylveon. Their sun core never got unstacked damage through — Heat Wave only hit Whimsicott/Kingambit into the Occa/Sash, my Zard resisted Flare Blitz, and Venusaur's Sleep Powder missed. By t8 the board was 2v1 and Weather Ball finished Sylveon. Costs: Whimsicott was a dead slot (Prankster Encore whiffed on Dark Incineroar twice, then died to Flare Blitz t3), and Garchomp ate Parting Shot + two Intimidates, ending asleep to Yawn when the game was already over.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Zard-Y + Garchomp lead structure and the Ancient Power/Earthquake pressure core. Fix Whimsicott's role: never Encore a Dark-type with Prankster — either lead Kingambit instead (Defiant turns Intimidate/Fake Out leads into +2 attack, and Occa Berry already survived the Heat Wave) or save Whimsicott for a Tailwind pivot. Expect opponent adaptations in game 2: Sylveon's unused Detect turn 1, Yawn sleep-fishing earlier, and Toxapex (WideGuard blocks my spread moves Earthquake/Rock Slide) or Choice Scarf Garchomp entering the four. Protect-call discipline: their Zard-Y Protect-stacked twice and lost to it — punish the pattern, but they may flip to Detect reads.
reflections.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon; series 1-0. G1 won via Ancient Power spread KOs (Incineroar t6, foe Zard-Y t8) + Rock Slide chip + Weather Ball clean on Sylveon. Their Zard-Y double-Protected then lost to the punish — pattern to exploit, watch for Detect instead. Sylveon Hyper Voice is 1x on Kingambit (36.2-52.7%): no safe switch-in. Damage anchors (sun): my Zard-Y Weather Ball 49.5-82.9% / Heat Wave 46.5-79.4% on Sylveon; Ancient Power 83-98% on foe Zard-Y; -2 Atk Garchomp Rock Slide 68-90% on foe Zard-Y, 10.4-20% on Sylveon; Sylveon Hyper Voice 71.8-107.7% on Garchomp. Sylveon: Quiet, Pixilate, Fairy Feather, Detect/Yawn/Quick Attack/Hyper Voice — Detect was never used in G1, likely t1 surprise; Yawn sleeps despite boosts. Prankster Encore is immune vs Dark Incineroar — never Encore it; Whimsicott died t3 to Flare Blitz, use it as late Tailwind pivot or bench for Kingambit. Incineroar Fake Out is an auto-lead threat; Kingambit (Defiant, Occa Berry survived sun Heat Wave 97->30%) is a strong answer/cleaner once Intimidate and Sylveon are handled. Unbenched game 2 candidates: Toxapex (WideGuard blocks Earthquake/Rock Slide — carry single-target coverage, e.g. Basculegion WaveCrash) and Choice Scarf Adamant Garchomp (outruns my Tailwind-less board; Stomping Tantrum/Earthquake/Dragon Claw/Rock Slide).

reflections.summary: The opening pressure was good, but Whimsicott still established Tailwind and the opponent stabilized with Charizard/Garchomp. Venusaur’s 75% Sleep Powder miss was a major swing, after which the opposing Charizard’s Ancient Power and Garchomp’s Rock Slide repeatedly covered our Charizard. A Rock Slide flinch and failed consecutive Protect accelerated the collapse. Sylveon’s Yawn neutralized Garchomp, but the faster opposing Charizard remained and finished Sylveon; selecting Hyper Voice rather than Quick Attack left the 4% Charizard alive for the KO.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Sylveon as the principal Garchomp/Kingambit answer and Incineroar as pivot/Fake Out utility, but do not expose our Charizard while both opposing Charizard and Garchomp are active. Consider Toxapex over Venusaur for Wide Guard/Toxic against Rock Slide, Earthquake and Heat Wave, reducing reliance on 75% Sleep Powder. If expecting the same Kingambit/Whimsicott lead, use a non-Intimidate lead or have a definite answer to +2 Kingambit. In the endgame, use Sylveon’s Quick Attack to remove weakened faster threats instead of defaulting to spread damage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s Game 1 selection was Kingambit, Whimsicott, Charizard and Garchomp, with Basculegion and Floette left out. They led Kingambit/Whimsicott, prioritized immediate Tailwind, and pivoted Charizard in to preserve Kingambit. Their Charizard/Garchomp core is willing to concentrate Rock Slide and Ancient Power on our Charizard, so bring ours in only after one is disabled. Incineroar safely absorbs Prankster Encore but activates Defiant on Kingambit; avoid giving Kingambit further drops through Parting Shot. Sylveon remains the answer to Garchomp and can pressure Kingambit, but should use Quick Attack against weakened faster targets. Planned change: consider Toxapex over Venusaur for Wide Guard/Toxic against the opponent’s spread offense.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard-Y + Whimsicott: Whimsicott is a Fake Out magnet (Sash absorbs it) and immune to Venusaur's Sleep Powder while Prankster Tailwind fixes sun-Chlorophyll speed; Charizard repeats the G1-winning Ancient Power punish on Zard-Y. Back Kingambit (Defiant absorbs Intimidate, Occa Berry survives Heat Wave, resists Sludge Bomb) as the cleaner with Basculegion's Water STAB covering Incineroar/Zard/Venusaur.
decisions.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Sylveon; series 1-0, G2 lead chosen: Charizard-Y + Whimsicott, back Kingambit + Basculegion. G1 won via Ancient Power spread KOs (Incineroar t6, foe Zard-Y t8) + Weather Ball clean on Sylveon. Their Zard-Y double-Protected then lost to the punish — expect Detect from Sylveon instead of Protect. Damage anchors (sun): my Zard-Y Weather Ball 49.5-82.9% / Heat Wave 46.5-79.4% on Sylveon; Ancient Power 83-98% on foe Zard-Y; -2 Atk Garchomp Rock Slide 68-90% on foe Zard-Y, 10.4-20% on Sylveon; Sylveon Hyper Voice 71.8-107.7% on Garchomp, 36.2-52.7% on Kingambit. Kingambit (Occa) survived sun Heat Wave 97->30% in G1; Defiant punishes Intimidate; Sludge Bomb only ~0.5x on it. Whimsicott: Grass = Sleep Powder immune, Sash, Prankster Tailwind beats sun-Chlorophyll Venusaur (184 > 200-264 doubled); Prankster Encore fails vs Dark Incineroar — never Encore it; it died t3 to Flare Blitz in G1, don't risk it past its job. Basculegion WaveCrash/AquaJet is the Water answer to Incineroar/Zard-Y; EQ pairs badly with Kingambit (2x on ally). Opponent likely repeats G1 four (Incineroar/Zard-Y/Venusaur/Sylveon); Toxapex (WideGuard) and Scarf Garchomp are the unbenched pivots if shown — carry single-target coverage vs Wide Guard. Fake Out lead expected: it can only flinch one — feed it to Whimsicott/Sash or Kingambit and act with the other.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar/Toxapex to delay an immediate Tailwind with Fake Out while Wide Guard, Toxic, and Baneful Bunker blunt the opponent’s spread and contact offense. Sylveon remains the midgame answer to Garchomp and Kingambit, while Mega Charizard is preserved for a late sweep after the opposing Rock Slide/Ancient Power users are disabled.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Game 1 selection was Kingambit, Whimsicott, Charizard and Garchomp, leaving out Basculegion and Floette-Eternal. decisions.rationale: Wide Guard blocks both spread options (Heat Wave/Ancient Power), so attacking into this lead is low-value; Mega+Protect guarantees Drought and keeps Zard safe whichever target Fake Out picks. If they Fake Out Zard, Prankster Tailwind lands; if they Fake Out Whimsicott, we lose tempo for one turn but Whimsicott, Sash and the Tailwind plan are intact (Fake Out won't break Sash). Never Encore Incineroar (Dark).

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Incineroar)
decisions.rationale: Fake Out Whimsicott denies the Prankster Tailwind that drove their Game 1 plan; Wide Guard then blocks Charizard's likely sun-boosted Heat Wave. Even if Charizard singles out Incineroar with Ancient Power, it only deals ~22-33%, safely healed by Sitrus, and Whimsicott's Focus Sash makes Toxic less urgent than protecting both slots this turn.

Tailwind first via Prankster (Fake Out can't target it twice; it resolves before any retaliation), and Ancient Power into Incineroar is Zard's only strong hit here (2x, ~34-61%) — Wide Guard repeat is a low-odds block, and Fake Out itself is unusable on cooldown.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on Whimsicott from 82% even after Intimidate, denying Tailwind unless they spend the turn on Protect/Encore (either way no Tailwind goes up, and Encore just forces a harmless pivot later). Beating Ancient Power on Incineroar: same guaranteed KO but Heat Wave adds guaranteed Toxapex chip in the Protect branch and is stronger vs Toxapex (21-37.6% vs 16-29%).

decisions.rationale: Incineroar is threatened by Wave Crash/Aqua Jet and Ancient Power under Tailwind and cannot Fake Out Ghost-type Basculegion, so Protect stalls a Tailwind turn while Charizard's toxic chip ticks. Toxapex walls everything on their side (resists all of Charizard's moves and Basculegion's Water STAB), so it doesn't need Baneful Bunker; Toxic on Basculegion puts their biggest physical threat on a timer alongside Charizard, letting Toxapex + Regenerator stall both out.

Basculegion's Wave Crash into the 70% Incineroar is ~94% to KO outright (66.8–122.4% range), avoids Baneful Bunker bait, and can't be blocked by Wide Guard; Zard's Heat Wave covers the failed-roll/Protect case, guarantees the KO, and chips Toxapex down to ~44–61% despite resistance. Fake Out is legal this turn but only threatens Zard, and losing one Heat Wave to a flinch is a cheap risk with the Wave Crash still landing; Zard's Protect isn't worth ceding the chip. Even if Incineroar Parting Shots, it drops a Special Attacker, not Basc's physical damage.

decisions.rationale: Both foes are badly poisoned and on a timer; my job is to stall. Incineroar (71%) can be KO'd by Wave Crash (64-95% range) and moves after everything under Tailwind, so Parting Shot/attacks are too slow and Protect may fail after last turn's use. Sylveon is the ideal pivot: Wave Crash cannot OHKO it (46-66%), Ancient Power only does 15-20%, and it resists Heat Wave; switching Charizard in would eat a 2x Wave Crash (70-167%), so that's out. Toxapex uses Baneful Bunker to guarantee its own safety from any targeted move while toxic ticks (Charizard to ~63%, Basculegion to ~80%) and Tailwind/Sun tick down. Incineroar is preserved for a later Intimidate + Fake Out re-entry.

Incineroar is the correct replacement: Intimidate neuters Basculegion's physical damage, it resists both foes' STABs, and Fake Out/Parting Shot buy stall turns. Our Charizard must stay benched — switching it in exposes it to Wave Crash and Ancient Power, and it serves as the late-game finisher once their checks are removed.

Their Charizard/Garchomp core concentrates Rock Slide and Ancient Power on our Charizard; never switch our Charizard into Basculegion (Wave Crash is 2x SE, 70%+) and keep it back as the finisher until Wave Crash/Ancient Power/Rock Slide users are removed. Game 2 validated the Toxapex stall plan: Toxic their Mega Charizard immediately on sight, Toxic Basculegion next, then alternate Baneful Bunker and Wide Guard (never consecutive Wide Guard) while Regenerator/Leftovers sustain; Wide Guard also covers Garchomp Earthquake which is 2x SE on Toxapex. Incineroar pairs with Toxapex as the disruption pivot: Intimidate, Fake Out to delay Tailwind, Flare Blitz OHKOs Whimsicott after Sash breaks, and it safely absorbs Prankster Encore (hard-switch if locked into Fake Out) — but avoid Parting Shot into Kingambit (Defiant). Sylveon answers Garchomp, pressures Kingambit, and walls Basculegion Wave Crash; use Quick Attack on weakened faster targets, and consider Detect more freely to let ally Wide Guard cover spread hits.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Incineroar: Wave Crash (43.6-82.4%) + Ancient Power (33.7-61.2%) sums to a guaranteed KO of the 70% Incineroar even at minimum rolls. Both are single-target, so Wide Guard is irrelevant, and Toxapex cannot Protect after using Baneful Bunker last turn. Ancient Power outdamages Heat Wave vs Incineroar (single-target 2x vs spread 0.5x) and still pressures Toxapex next turn; removing Incineroar first eliminates Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot pivots before their 4th member arrives.
decisions.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Toxapex; series 1-0, game 2 in progress. Basculegion: WaveCrash/AquaJet 2x on Incineroar and Zard-Y; near-useless vs Toxapex (0.5x) — vs Toxapex use Zard Heat Wave or pivot Kingambit Iron Head. Wave Crash vs Incineroar at 0 atk 66.8-122.4% (LO Adaptability); at -1 atk 43.6-82.4%. Zard-Y Ancient Power vs Incineroar 2x 33.7-61.2%; vs Toxapex ~15.9-28.8%; Heat Wave vs Toxapex 21.0-37.6%, vs Incineroar 22.3-40% (spread). Ancient Power + Wave Crash double into healthy Incineroar is a guaranteed KO. Kingambit (Occa, survived sun Heat Wave 97->30% in G1): 0.25x Sylveon Hyper Voice, 0.5x Sludge Bomb/Heat Wave, Defiant punishes Intimidate/Parting Shot; Low Kick 2x Incineroar; weak to Scarf Garchomp EQ — keep away if Garchomp revealed. Prankster Encore fails vs Dark — never Encore Incineroar. Toxapex consecutive Wide Guard only ~1/3 success; single-target moves Wide-Guard-proof; Basc is Bunker-bait — target Incineroar to dodge Bunker. Fake Out only threatens Zard (Basc Ghost-immune, unflinchable); Incineroar Fake Out has 1-turn gap. Expect foe's remaining unrevealed member among Garchomp/Charizard-Y/Venusaur; watch Parting Shot pivot — harmless if Incineroar dies first. Both our mons are badly poisoned: plan for ~1/8 end-of-turn chip; Zard also has Wave Crash recoil to track on Basc (56% -> don't stack recoil unless KOing).

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Incineroar)
decisions.rationale: Both foes are badly poisoned and toxic is ramping (Charizard faints ~turn 7, Basculegion ~turn 6-7 if untouched). Wave Crash OHKOs Incineroar even at -1 (Life Orb Adaptability 2x SE), and Aqua Jet + Heat Wave could also KO, so Incineroar must Protect (fresh since its last Protect was turn 3). Wide Guard covers Charizard's Heat Wave for Toxapex; even if it failed from the shared protect counter, Toxapex resists everything they can throw. End of turn: both foes take another toxic tick, and Tailwind + Sun both expire, leaving them slowed with Drought gone and the stall fully in our favor. Never switch Charizard into Basculegion.

Basculegion's Wave Crash is a guaranteed KO on Incineroar from 70% (90.1-165.3% range; recoil capped at ~1/3 of its remaining 70% ≈ Basc survives). Incineroar will Fake Out Zard at +3 priority before Basc connects, so Zard Protects to eat the Fake Out safely instead of wasting Ancient Power on a target that's already being KO'd. Even Incineroar's consecutive-turn Protect only saves it ~1/3 of the time.
decisions.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Toxapex; series 1-0, game 2 in progress. Basc: WaveCrash/AquaJet 2x on Incineroar and Zard-Y; near-useless vs Toxapex (0.5x) — vs Toxapex use Zard Heat Wave or pivot Kingambit Iron Head (Steel 2x on Poison). Wave Crash vs Incineroar at 0 atk 66.8-122.4%; at -1 atk 90.1-165.3% (LO Adaptability) — GUARANTEED KO from full, recoil on KO capped at ~1/3 of Incineroar's remaining HP (Basc survives). Zard-Y Ancient Power vs Incineroar 2x 33.7-61.2%; vs Toxapex ~15.9-28.8%; Heat Wave vs Toxapex 21.0-37.6%, vs Incineroar 22.3-40% (spread). Kingambit (Occa, survived sun Heat Wave 97->30% in G1): 0.25x Sylveon Hyper Voice, 0.5x Sludge Bomb/Heat Wave, Defiant punishes Intimidate/Parting Shot; Low Kick 2x Incineroar; weak to Scarf Garchomp EQ — keep away if Garchomp revealed. Prankster Encore fails vs Dark — never Encore Incineroar. Toxapex consecutive Wide Guard/Bunker only ~1/3 success; single-target moves Wide-Guard-proof; Basc is Bunker-bait — target Incineroar to dodge Bunker. Fake Out only threatens Zard (Basc Ghost-immune, unflinchable). If Incineroar Parting Shots instead, our declared attacks hit its replacement (Wave Crash neutral Garchomp, 2x Zard-Y, 0.5x Venusaur). Foe's unrevealed 4th: Garchomp (Scarf 122-154, EQ 2x Zard, weak Kingambit) / Charizard-Y (sun) / Venusaur (Focus Sash, Sleep Powder). Both Zard and Basc badly poisoned: ~1/8 end-of-turn chip; don't stack Wave Crash recoil unnecessarily. Whimsicott dead (1 fallen boosts Last Respects +20).

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Both foes are on lethal toxic timers (Charizard ~41%, Basculegion ~37%) and our Protect/Wide Guard are both on reduced success from last turn, so I avoid consecutive-protection failure: Toxapex uses a fresh Baneful Bunker to stay safe while Incineroar chips Charizard with Flare Blitz to push it into end-of-turn toxic KO range, removing the Ancient Power threat. Even if Incineroar is focused down, toxic (plus Life Orb) finishes both foes while healthy Toxapex stalls Basculegion, keeping our Charizard in back until Basculegion is gone.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

My Zard-Y dies to toxic at end of turn regardless, so it must spend its last action on its only real damage: Ancient Power is 4x into the foe Charizard (75.7-143.8%, possible OHKO). Foe Charizard has saved its Mega all game; if it Mega Evolves now, sun Heat Wave KOs Kingambit even through Occa Berry, so removing the Charizard is the only win line. Kingambit's Sucker Punch (+1 priority) always resolves before the foe's Heat Wave even at Speed 70, and combined the double-target is a guaranteed KO if neither move is blocked (75.7+34.1 > 100% at minimums). Toxapex cannot threaten Kingambit at all (Steel is Toxic-immune; all its moves are 0.5x/negligible), so targeting it has no value.
decisions.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Toxapex; series 1-0. Game 2 likely lost if foe Charizard Mega Evolves: sun Heat Wave OHKOs Kingambit even through Occa (Occa halves but ~2x sun spread Fire still exceeds 207 HP), and my Zard-Y cannot survive toxic ticks past turn 7 (4/16 tick > remaining HP). Key damage facts: my Zard-Y Ancient Power 4x into foe Charizard 75.7-143.8% (possible OHKO from full); Kingambit Sucker Punch into foe Charizard 34.1-64.7%; Sucker Punch priority beats all priority-0 moves, so it lands before foe Heat Wave despite Kingambit's 70 Speed. Sucker Punch fails if the target selects a non-damaging move (Protect/Bunker). Toxapex does nothing to Kingambit: Steel immune to Toxic/Baneful Bunker poison, Iron Head/Low Kick 0.5x, Kowtow Cleave ~10% per hit vs its bulk — Kingambit walls Toxapex indefinitely. Toxapex consecutive Protect-style moves only ~1/3 success. Foe's unrevealed 4th team member: Garchomp (Scarf 122-154, EQ 2x Zard, weak Kingambit) or Venusaur (Focus Sash, Sleep Powder); assume Chlorophyll Venusaur pairs with sun. In game 3, if I bring Charizard-Y I should Mega immediately (foe hoarded theirs for a late sweep) and preserve Kingambit against sun Fire spreads; Basculegion Wave Crash guaranteed KOs Incineroar from full (recoil-capped, survives); never Encore Incineroar with Prankster; target Incineroar around Baneful Bunker; Whimsicott dead boosts Last Respects by +20 per fallen ally.

decisions.rationale: Foe Charizard-Mega-Y is at 12% with bad poison at a high toxic counter — it faints to the end-of-turn tick no matter what, so this turn is free. Kingambit is Steel-type: immune to Toxic and Baneful Bunker's poison, so Toxapex instead lands Infestation on Kingambit for trap chip (resisted direct damage but the 1/8-per-turn residual is our only residual option vs Steel). My Charizard Protects to blank any double-target from Kingambit + Ancient Power while Mega Evolving now: Drought sun sets up a boosted Weather Ball/Heat Wave finish on Kingambit next turn in the 2v1. Heat Wave can't OHKO through Occa Berry even in sun, so I take the zero-risk line: Protect this turn, then sun-boosted single-target Weather Ball into Kingambit on turn 8 with Toxapex (which resists Kingambit's entire kit) as backup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent adapts lineup between games: Game 1 was Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard/Garchomp, Game 2 was Whimsicott/Charizard/Basculegion/Kingambit, so Game 3 likely keeps the Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard core with either Garchomp, Basculegion, or Floette-E as the flex. Their Charizard/Garchomp core concentrates Rock Slide and Ancient Power on our Charizard; never switch our Charizard into Basculegion (Wave Crash 2x SE, 70%+) and keep it back as finisher until Wave Crash/Ancient Power/Rock Slide users are gone. Toxapex stall plan validated: Toxic their Mega Charizard on sight, Toxic Basculegion next, alternate Baneful Bunker and Wide Guard (never consecutive Wide Guard) with Regenerator/Leftovers sustain; Wide Guard covers Garchomp Earthquake (2x SE on Toxapex). Kingambit is Steel: IMMUNE to Toxic and Baneful Bunker poison — vs Kingambit use Infestation for trap chip and let Charizard's sun-boosted Weather Ball/Heat Wave (2x SE) do the real damage; Kingambit carries Occa Berry so fire moves won't OHKO from full, plan for two hits. Never Parting Shot into Kingambit (Defiant). Incineroar pairs with Toxapex: Intimidate, Fake Out to delay Tailwind, Flare Blitz OHKOs Whimsicott after Sash breaks, safely absorbs Prankster Encore (hard-switch if locked into Fake Out). Sylveon answers Garchomp, pressures Kingambit, walls Basculegion Wave Crash; Quick Attack on weakened faster targets, Detect freely while ally Wide Guard covers spread.

decisions.rationale: Zard-Y is gone; slot 1 passes. I cannot KO the foe's 100% Zard-Y this turn (Kowtow 41-78%, Sucker 34-65%), but Occa + spread reduction caps its Heat Wave at 66.7-91.8% of Kingambit's max, so Kingambit survives ~73% of rolls (plus 10% miss). Zard-Y always moves first, so max damage before it acts: Kowtow Cleave now (leaves Zard 22-59%), banking Sucker Punch's +1 priority for turn 9 to strike before the now-Occa-less Heat Wave and try for the KO. Sucker now would leave Zard too high for the guaranteed turn-9 Sucker to finish. If the Heat Wave roll is high or Zard Protects, game 2 is lost, but this is the only winning line.
decisions.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Toxapex; series 1-0, game 2 in progress (lost if this line fails). DURABLE DAMAGE FACTS: foe Zard-Y Heat Wave into my Kingambit with Occa Berry and spread reduction: 66.7-91.8% of max (NOT guaranteed through Occa when Kingambit above ~92%); without Occa it is a guaranteed OHKO, so never let Kingambit eat a second sun Fire spread. My Kingambit into foe Zard-Y: Kowtow Cleave 41.1-78.4%, Sucker Punch 34.1-64.7% (no OHKO from full); Sucker's +1 beats all priority-0 moves but fails vs Protect/Bunker; foe Zard Protect turn 1 with Incineroar Fake Out lead. My Zard-Y Ancient Power 75.7-143.8% into foe Zard-Y (possible OHKO from full); my Zard-Y Speed 167 exact, foe range 132-167. Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees KO on Incineroar from full (recoil-capped, survives); never Encore Incineroar with Prankster; attack around Baneful Bunker. Toxapex: Steel immune to Toxic/Bunker poison, Kingambit walls it forever; its consecutive Protect-style moves ~1/3 success; Regenerator+Leftovers stall — must be pressured by strong physical hits, not chipped. Foe hoards Mega Zard-Y for late game and won it via sun Fire spreads + Toxic chip in game 2. Game 3 plan: bring Charizard-Y and Mega immediately (do not mirror their late Mega), preserve Kingambit from sun Fire spreads (Occa only buys one Heat Wave), lead around Fake Out/Protect, keep Basculegion for Incineroar; Whimsicott Tailwind useful but never Encore Incineroar; if game 2 line succeeded, Zard-Y mirror resolved by Ancient Power + Sucker Punch pressure.

decisions.rationale: Weather Ball is the strongest accurate sun-boosted Fire hit into Kingambit even after Occa Berry; Kingambit's Sucker Punch/Kowtow cannot OHKO Charizard from full, while Toxapex Infestation adds safe chip/trap if Charizard rolls low.

reflections.summary: Lost in 8 turns to a Protect-and-chip war of attrition. Whimsicott was flinched by Fake Out on turn 1 and died to Flare Blitz on turn 2, leaving us one Pokémon down before we ever moved it meaningfully. Both Charizard and Basculegion then got Toxic'd, and the opponent's rotation (Incineroar Protect spam, Baneful Bunker, Wide Guard, sacrificial Sylveon, Intimidate pivot) invalidated almost every attacking turn: turns 3 and 5 were nearly fully blanked by Protect. We still won the exchange trade (Sylveon and Incineroar KO'd), but poison ticks plus Life Orb/recoil finished Basculegion and poison finished our Charizard on turn 7, leaving Kingambit alone against a full-HP Toxapex and full-HP Zard-Y. Critical new fact: sun Weather Ball KO'd Kingambit through the Occa Berry from ~85%, so Occa only guards Heat Wave, not sun Weather Ball. No decision errors were logged; the loss was structural — early 4-to-3, Toxic on both attackers, and Protect nullifying offense.
reflections.adjustment: Game 3 is the decider against the same six. Lead to deny the Fake Out/Protect tempo grab: our own Fake Out-punishing options are limited, so either lead Charizard-Y + Basculegion (both threaten Incineroar hard and don't care about Fake Out) or accept Whimsicott as a Tailwind/Encore sacrifice but don't rely on it. Never let both attackers get Toxic'd — pressure Toxapex immediately with Kingambit's physical hits (it walls Toxic/Bunker completely) before their Zard-Y arrives. Treat Kingambit as one Heat Wave only: sun Weather Ball is a certain KO through Occa, so don't let Kingambit face Zard-Y while sun is up unless Kowtow Cleave range is confirmed. Their Protect spam means any predictable single-target offense gets blanked — attack the non-Protect side, and remember their consecutive Protect-style moves fail about a third of the time. Mirror their early Mega rather than hoarding ours: their late Zard-Y was clean last game; ours dying to poison before it could matter was the swing.
reflections.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Toxapex; series 1-1, game 3 is the decider. DURABLE DAMAGE FACTS: sun Weather Ball KOs my Kingambit through Occa Berry from ~85% (Occa guards Heat Wave only, never sun Weather Ball); without sun-mega-Fire, never leave Kingambit in vs their Zard-Y. Foe Zard-Y Heat Wave with Occa: 66.7-91.8% (not guaranteed); without Occa guaranteed OHKO. My Kingambit into foe Zard-Y: Kowtow 41.1-78.4%, Sucker 34.1-64.7%, no OHKO; Sucker +1 fails vs Protect/Bunker. My Zard-Y Ancient Power 75.7-143.8% into foe Zard-Y (possible OHKO); Speed 167 exact vs foe 132-167. Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees KO on Incineroar from full, survives; never Encore Incineroar with Prankster. OPPONENT TENDENCIES (confirmed both games): leads Incineroar/Toxapex and Protects turn 1 with Zard-Y; Incineroar spams Protect (failed our attacks turns 3 and 5); hoards Mega Zard-Y for the late game and wins via sun Fire spreads + Toxic chip; rotates Incineroar back in mid-game for a second Intimidate; uses Toxapex (Wide Guard/Bunker/Toxic + Regenerator stall) as the Protect engine, sacrificing Sylveon freely; consecutive Protect-style moves ~1/3 fail rate. Toxapex: Kingambit immune to Toxic/Bunker and walls it — best early physical pressure source. PLAN for game 3: Mega Charizard-Y immediately (no late mirror), lead around Fake Out (prefer Charizard+Basculegion or accept Whimsicott loss), rush Toxapex with Kingambit before their Zard-Y enters, avoid double-Toxic on my attackers, never let Kingambit eat sun Weather Ball.

reflections.summary: Won by executing the Toxic-stall gameplan exactly as planned: Fake Out delayed Whimsicott's Tailwind while Flare Blitz removed it, Toxapex landed Toxic on their Mega Charizard (T2) and Basculegion (T3), and layered Protect/Baneful Bunker/Wide Guard turns let poison do the work — Basculegion and their Charizard both died to Toxic without needing to be KO'd. Endgame vs Kingambit followed the plan: no Parting Shot into Defiant, Infestation chip + trap, Protect baited a failed Sucker Punch, then sun-boosted Weather Ball finished Kingambit through Occa Berry from 85%. Only real cost was Sylveon, doubled into and KO'd on its switch-in turn (Heat Wave + Wave Crash), and one failed Baneful Bunker after Wide Guard (consecutive protect-family fail).
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Toxic-stall core and the Kingambit endgame sequence — both validated. For game 3: (1) don't hard-switch Sylveon into a turn where the opponent can double that slot; either Protect/Detect the pivot turn or bring it in on a guaranteed free switch, since this opponent aggressively doubles predicted switch-ins. (2) Never run Baneful Bunker immediately after Wide Guard — insert an attack turn between protect-family moves to avoid the fail chance that already occurred once. (3) Expect adaptation: with Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard locked, their flex slot may become Floette-E or Garchomp, and they may lead Kingambit since it's Toxic-immune — if so, skip Toxic, open with Infestation chip and pressure with fire coverage while keeping our Charizard in back as the finisher.
reflections.notebook: Opponent adapts lineup between games: Game 1 was Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard/Garchomp, Game 2 was Whimsicott/Charizard/Basculegion/Kingambit, so Game 3 likely keeps the Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard core with either Garchomp, Basculegion, or Floette-E as the flex. Their Charizard runs Ancient Power as Rock coverage and will click it repeatedly into our side; never switch our Charizard into it, Basculegion Wave Crash (2x SE), or Garchomp Rock Slide — keep our Zard as the backline finisher. Toxapex stall plan validated twice: Toxic their Mega Charizard on sight (they let it die to poison rather than preserve it), Toxic Basculegion next, alternate Baneful Bunker and Wide Guard with an attack turn in between (protect-family moves fail consecutively — happened in game 2) with Regenerator/Leftovers sustain; Wide Guard covers Garchomp Earthquake. Kingambit is Steel: IMMUNE to Toxic and Baneful Bunker poison — vs Kingambit use Infestation for trap chip and let Charizard's sun Weather Ball/Heat Wave do the damage; Kingambit has Occa Berry but sun Weather Ball still KO'd from 85%, so one chip + one hit suffices; they click Sucker Punch reactively — Protect baits it. Never Parting Shot into Kingambit (Defiant). Incineroar pairs with Toxapex: Intimidate, Fake Out delays Tailwind, Flare Blitz KO's Whimsicott once Sash is chipped, absorbs Prankster Encore (hard-switch if locked). Sylveon answers Garchomp, pressures Kingambit, walls Basculegion Wave Crash — but opponent aggressively doubles predicted switch-in slots (Sylveon was doubled and KO'd on entry in game 2), so only pivot it in on guaranteed free turns or behind Detect/Wide Guard cover.

decisions.rationale: Lead Basculegion (Ghost-immune to their Fake Out, guaranteed Wave Crash KO on Incineroar from full) with Kingambit to rush Toxapex before their hoarded Zard-Y enters; back Charizard (immediate Mega) + Whimsicott (Tailwind/Encore support).
decisions.notebook: Series 332b0103336f vs sun core (Zard-Y/Venusaur) + Incineroar + Toxapex; series 1-1, game 3 decider. DURABLE DAMAGE FACTS: sun Weather Ball KOs my Kingambit through Occa Berry from ~85% (Occa guards Heat Wave only, never sun Weather Ball); without sun-mega-Fire, never leave Kingambit in vs their Zard-Y. Foe Zard-Y Heat Wave with Occa: 66.7-91.8% (not guaranteed); without Occa guaranteed OHKO. My Kingambit into foe Zard-Y: Kowtow 41.1-78.4%, Sucker 34.1-64.7%, no OHKO; Sucker +1 fails vs Protect/Bunker. My Zard-Y Ancient Power 75.7-143.8% into foe Zard-Y (possible OHKO); my Zard Speed 167 exact vs foe 132-167. Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees KO on Incineroar from full, survives; never Encore Incineroar with Prankster; Basculegion immune to their Fake Out. OPPONENT TENDENCIES (confirmed both games): leads Incineroar/Toxapex and Protects turn 1 with Zard-Y; Incineroar spams Protect; hoards Mega Zard-Y for late game, wins via sun Fire spreads + Toxic chip; rotates Incineroar back mid-game for second Intimidate; Toxapex is Protect engine (Wide Guard/Bunker/Toxic + Regenerator), sacrifices Sylveon freely; consecutive Protect-style moves ~1/3 fail. Toxapex: Kingambit immune to Toxic/Bunker and walls it — best early physical pressure. GAME 3 PLAN: lead Basculegion + Kingambit; Mega Charizard-Y immediately whenever it enters (no late mirror); rush Toxapex with Kingambit before their Zard-Y enters; avoid double-Toxic on my attackers; never let Kingambit eat sun Weather Ball.

decisions.rationale: Run the twice-validated core: Incineroar+Toxapex lead (Intimidate, Fake Out to delay Tailwind, Toxic/Baneful Bunker/Wide Guard stall), Mega Charizard-Y as protected backline finisher (never switch it into Ancient Power/Wave Crash/Rock Slide). Fourth slot goes to Venusaur over Sylveon: Sylveon was read and double-targeted on entry in game 2, while Venusaur brings Focus Sash safety, Chlorophyll speed under our own sun, Earth Power for Kingambit (which is immune to Toxic), and Sleep Powder pressure. Garchomp is left home since Toxapex Wide Guard already covers opposing Earthquake and our answers to their Garchomp are covered.
decisions.notebook: Opponent adapts lineup between games: Game 1 was Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard/Garchomp, Game 2 was Whimsicott/Charizard/Basculegion/Kingambit, so Game 3 likely keeps the Kingambit/Whimsicott/Charizard core with either Garchomp, Basculegion, or Floette-E as the flex. Their Charizard runs Ancient Power as Rock coverage and will click it repeatedly into our side; never switch our Charizard into it, Basculegion Wave Crash (2x SE), or Garchomp Rock Slide — keep our Zard as the backline finisher. Toxapex stall plan validated twice: Toxic their Mega Charizard on sight (they let it die to poison rather than preserve it), Toxic Basculegion next, alternate Baneful Bunker and Wide Guard with an attack turn in between (protect-family moves fail consecutively — happened in game 2) with Regenerator/Leftovers sustain; Wide Guard covers Garchomp Earthquake. Kingambit is Steel: IMMUNE to Toxic and Baneful Bunker poison — vs Kingambit use Infestation for trap chip and let Charizard's sun Weather Ball/Heat Wave do the damage; Kingambit has Occa Berry but sun Weather Ball still KO'd from 85%, so one chip + one hit suffices; they click Sucker Punch reactively — Protect baits it. Never Parting Shot into Kingambit (Defiant). Incineroar pairs with Toxapex: Intimidate, Fake Out delays Tailwind, Flare Blitz KO's Whimsicott once Sash is chipped, absorbs Prankster Encore (hard-switch if locked). Sylveon answers Garchomp, pressures Kingambit, walls Basculegion Wave Crash — but opponent aggressively doubles predicted switch-in slots (Sylveon was doubled and KO'd on entry in game 2), so only pivot it in on guaranteed free turns or behind Detect/Wide Guard cover.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion outspeeds both foes: Wave Crash threatens a ~87% OHKO on Incineroar (90.1-165.3% before Sitrus; sub-100 rolls leave it under 35% and recoil only applies on hit, nothing if it Protects). Their confirmed pattern is Fake Out on turn 1, which lands before everything and will flinch Kingambit regardless of its move, so Kingambit's pick is nearly free — Kowtow Cleave into Toxapex (42.7-74.4%, neutral) applies planned pressure, and Kingambit is immune to both Bunker poison and Toxic if Toxapex bunker/Toxics instead. If Incineroar Protects instead, Kingambit still connects on Toxapex.

TURN 2 PLAN: Fake Out is spent (Incineroar must Protect/Parting Shot/Flare Blitz); if Incineroar alive, finish with Basc Aqua Jet/Wave Crash or Kingambit; keep pressuring Toxapex; if they bring Zard-Y, Mega my Zard-Y same turn and never keep Kingambit in against it; watch Wide Guard — it blocks spread moves only, my moves are single-target.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out flinches +1 Kingambit (immune option on Basculegion is useless) to neutralize its Defiant-boosted attack this turn while Toxapex lands Toxic on Basculegion per the validated stall plan; if Basculegion Protects, its Protect is burned and Kingambit still loses the turn, and we re-Toxic next turn. Avoid Parting Shot into Kingambit (Defiant) and Toxic into Kingambit (Steel immunity).

Venusaur outspeeds both active foes, can immediately Sleep Powder Kingambit or pressure with Earth Power, while Focus Sash guards against a single hit; Charizard remains preserved as the backline finisher.

Basculegion Protects (+4 priority, always first) — it is toxic'd at 50% and its Water moves are resisted by both foes, so it cannot contribute safely. Kingambit (+1) Kowtow Cleaves Venusaur (58.3–109% through Focus Sash's 1 HP floor; Venusaur never outspeeds Kingambit but always acts first — worst case Earth Power does 41.5–61.8% and Kingambit survives, best case Venusaur is left at 1–42% in Sucker Punch KO range next turn). I deliberately keep my Zard-Y benched: mega-ing now triggers my Drought, which doubles their Chlorophyll Venusaur to 200–264 Speed, letting it Sleep Powder my Charizard freely — a mirror disaster. Toxapex is left alone this turn since it most likely uses Baneful Bunker, and Kingambit stays as the healthy anti-Toxapex/Sylveon pivot.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit is the real threat (Steel, immune to Toxic/Baneful poison; Basculegion is already badly poisoned and dying to ticks). Venusaur's Sleep Powder is legal into Kingambit (Occa Berry, not Grass/Overcoat/Goggles) and has a key synergy: if they click Sucker Punch predicting Earth Power, it fails against a status move. If sleep lands, Kingambit is neutralized while Infestation traps it (no switch-out) and stacks 12.5%/turn chip, letting Venusaur Earth Power (40-73% per hit) finish it safely next turns. Even on a miss or a Kowtow Cleave into Venusaur, Focus Sash keeps Venusaur alive. Toxapex takes little from either foe (Wave Crash/Iron Head resisted), so Infestation chip + trap beats Baneful Bunker here.

Kingambit can still be asleep, but if it wakes (~1/3), Kowtow breaks Venusaur's sash (58.3-109%) or KOs. Basculegion (-1, resisted by both foes, 37% toxic'd, Earth Power 24.6-36.4% can KO after chip) is worth more benched than attacking; Whimsicott absorbs Sleep Powder, sashes vs Sludge Bomb/Earth Power, and sets Encore/Tailwind next turn while Kingambit keeps Infestation pressure. Kingambit survives even max Earth Power from 81%.

reflections.summary: Won 2-1. Game 3 was a war of attrition that our damage economy won. Early game went badly: Basculegion's Wave Crash opened by removing Incineroar (Defiant had already turned Intimidate into a free +2 for Kingambit), but Toxic on Basculegion, a Sleep Powder on Kingambit, and an Encore-locked Venusaur spamming Earth Power into Kingambit cost us our Adamant sweeper by turn 4 — Kingambit died asleep doing nothing after turn 1, so the Intimidate boost was wasted. From turn 5 onward the plan worked: Mega Zard-Y + Whimsicott killed Venusaur with a sun-boosted Weather Ball and then removed the opposing Mega Zard-Y outright with super-effective Ancient Power (2x on Fire/Flying — the right call over Weather Ball once our sun control mattered less). Whimsicott's Encore on Toxapex was the decisive play: locking Baneful Bunker meant it failed outright on the follow-up turns (Encore forces the move, and a forced protect-style use that violates the streak just fails), giving free damage turns. Whimsicott and eventually our Zard-Y succumbed to Toxic ticks, but Basculegion returned at 37% and Last Respects — scaling with our four faints plus Basculegion's own Life Orb — finished the lone Toxapex, which had no partner left and could only heal with Leftovers. No decision errors; the win came from refusing bad trades, timing Encore on the Protect spam, and out-damaging a solo wall while both sides bled from Toxic.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the team unchanged for the next round. Two habits to preserve: (a) when a lone protective wall is the only thing between you and the win, Encore its Protect-style move rather than attacking into it — a forced protect-style move failing outright converts tempo directly into damage turns; (b) treat a Toxic'd Pokémon's final tick as spent — give it maximum offensive value on that turn rather than protecting. One caution to carry forward: Kingambit opened gloriously on paper (Defiant flipping Intimidate) but never acted again after turn 1; against sleep/Encore disruption, don't let a boosted attacker sit passive — plan for it to be disabled and have Basculegion carry the tempo from the start.
reflections.notebook: DURABLE TEAM LESSONS (fixed 6: Kingambit/Basculegion/Garchomp/Zard-Y/Whimsicott/Floette-E): (1) Last Respects + Adaptability Basculegion (Life Orb) is the win condition — BP scales with total faints, so time a late-game return: 150 BP at 5 faints vastly outdamaged even resisted Wave Crash into bulky resists (roughly 76-133% vs 31-54% in that matchup). Frontload faints are a resource, not a loss. (2) Whimsicott Encore is the anti-wall tool: Encore-locked onto a Protect-style move, the target's forced repeat fails outright when the consecutive-use streak breaks — that yields guaranteed free turns for a double-attack squeeze. Protect-streak itself: after a successful use, next use ~1/3; after a fail, next use is free. (3) Zard-Y: Ancient Power beats Weather Ball/Heat Wave whenever weather is off — 60 BP 100% accurate, and it's the nuke vs Fire/Flying targets (2x). Keep sun for Weather Ball turns only. (4) Toxic management: assume the counter softens on re-entry (benched toxed mon ticked ~1/16 after returning) — a returning toxed sweeper buys extra clock, so use the bench strategically. A toxed mon at ~13% is dead to the tick: spend it attacking, never on Protect. (5) Wide Guard only stops spread; protect-style stops only single-target attacks — combined single-target pressure (two attackers) is the universal answer to defensive shells. (6) Defiant converts Intimidate leads into a +2 Kingambit, but sleep/Encore disruption can zero that out — don't rely on the boosted mode acting; Basculegion must be ready to carry from turn 1. (7) Encored attackers (Venusaur locked into Earth Power) are predictable damage sinks — Encore-protect them and switch around their fixed target. These damage/matchup numbers were observed vs this series' teams; recalibrate against new foes.

retrospective.didWell: The turn 1 Toxic on Basculegion was a strong long-term play that put a hard clock on the opponent's biggest threat, and Sleep Powder plus double Infestation chip let me remove a +2 Defiant Kingambit without it ever attacking. Toxapex's Baneful Bunker stalls on turns 7 and 9 correctly burned toxic turns on both enemy attackers, nearly running Charizard out of health via poison alone.
retrospective.didPoorly: Leading Incineroar into Basculegion/Kingambit was costly: Intimidate fed Defiant, Fake Out was resisted for 4%, and Incineroar died to Wave Crash for almost no value. On turn 5 I attacked with Venusaur instead of Protecting, so its Focus Sash never triggered and it fell to Weather Ball; on turn 6 I failed to Protect my own Charizard into the obvious Ancient Power, losing my Mega before it ever moved. Once Toxapex was Encored into Baneful Bunker with no teammates left to switch to, the endgame was purely procedural.
retrospective.wouldChange: Change the lead so Intimidate doesn't hand Kingambit a free Defiant boost, e.g. open Venusaur/Toxapex and keep Incineroar in back for a later pivot. Protect Venusaur on turn 5 (or Sleep Powder the incoming Charizard) to preserve the Focus Sash and keep a second attacker alive. Protect my Charizard on turn 6 against the mirror Charizard's Ancient Power rather than letting it faint before attacking. Reconsider the team-of-four selection, since Choice Scarf Garchomp or Sylveon likely matched up better into Basculegion/Charizard than the Charizard mirror that never fired a shot.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler+Lycanroc to Fake Out Whimsicott (deny Tailwind) and 4x Accelerock Charizard. Froslass is the Garchomp check and delayed-mega snow/Veil; Bascu is the Last Respects wincon. Bench Kingambit (4x Low Kick, 2x Fire/EQ) and Scovillain.
decisions.notebook: G1 plan: mega Froslass only (not Scovillain). Delay mega until after Charizard-Y Drought so snow overwrites; switch-in+mega+Veil same turn is legal. Sneasler Fake Out Whimsicott T1; Unburden via CC+White Herb. Lycanroc (sash, TC Accelerock) is the Charizard answer. Froslass Blizzard 4x Garchomp. Bascu Last Respects endgame; Wave Crash is sun-halved so do not rely on it vs Mega Y. Opp likely Charizard-Y+Whimsicott+Garchomp+Kingambit/Bascu; Fairy Aura Floette is the other mega. Opp has no Fake Out. If G2 they show no Charizard, lead Froslass and mega T1.

decisions.rationale: Deny Froslass snow/a veil with Charizard-Y Drought (speed order Froslass faster so Drought overwrites), Whimsicott Tailwind + Grass immunity to Scovillain Rage Powder + Encore on SD/Veil, Garchomp LO EQ/RSlide for Kingambit/Lycanroc/Scovillain (Rock Slide 2x Scovillain) and fast Tailwind abuse 169, Basculegion immune to Sneasler/Lycanroc CC, resists Ice, Aqua Jet priority and Ghost LastRespects 2x vs Froslass. Dropping our Kingambit (4x CC weak) and Floette (mega conflict with Y) gives best type/weather coverage.
decisions.notebook: Plan vs snow/veil: Charizard-Y Drought overwrites Froslass-Mega Snow Warning (Froslass 154-189 faster so Drought last). Whimsicott 184 Prankster Tailwind + Sash + Rage Powder immunity (Grass) + Encore vs SD/Veil. Basculegion Water/Ghost immune to Close Combat (Sneasler/Lycanroc) and resists Ice/Blizzard, Aqua Jet prio. Garchomp 169 LO EQ 2x Kingambit/Lycanroc, RSlide 2x Scovillain. Opponent has dual megas (Froslassite Snow Warning/Blizzard/Veil and Scovillainite Spicy Spray burn on hit) but only one can mega; Scovillain Chlorophyll speed doubled in our sun if they stay non-mega. Bring Y over Floette for weather control.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out Garchomp stops the spread EQ that OHKOs Sneasler; Lycanroc 162 always outspeeds Charizard and Accelerock (TC, STAB, 4x, 100%) is the reliable Mega-Y KO that also beats Protect-on-Garchomp. Doubling Charizard is punished by Protect+EQ.
decisions.notebook: G1: mega Froslass only. Delay mega until after Charizard-Y Drought so Snow overwrites; switch-in+mega+Veil same turn is legal. Sneasler Unburden via CC+White Herb after Fake Out is spent. Lycanroc (sash, TC Accelerock) is the Charizard answer; do not throw sash into EQ if Zard can still act. Froslass Blizzard 4x Garchomp. Bascu Last Respects endgame; Wave Crash is sun-halved vs Mega Y. Opp brought Garchomp+Charizard-Y plus 2 of Kingambit/Whimsicott/Bascu/Floette-Eternal; no Fake Out. If a later game they show no Charizard, lead Froslass and mega T1.

decisions.rationale: EQ is 2x to both foes 95-191% Sneasler and 94-187% Lycanroc (sash) while Rock Slide 4x 80-120% threatens Charizard; Charizard Protect+Mega blocks Rock Slide/Accelerock and Fake Out on that slot, still sets Drought before Heat Wave timing and blocks ally EQ, preserving weather control vs Froslass-Mega snow. If they Fake Out Garchomp EQ is stopped but Charizard safe + sun; if they Fake Out Charizard Protect blocks and EQ devastates.

Protect Sneasler from guaranteed EQ KO; priority TC Accelerock almost certainly KOs Mega Y (only an impractical max-Def spread lives) before it can punish sash. EQ then only sashes Lycanroc. Beats EQ+Heat Wave/Weather Ball and Garchomp Protect.

Garchomp EQ is guaranteed KO on Sneasler 87% (95.7% min) and 94.5% min on Lycanroc to break Sash. EQ hits Charizard-Y as immune (Flying), but hits any switched-in ally - Whimsicott takes 34-40% resisted vs Basculegion 37-71% making Whimsicott safer (max 89.8% with Rock 33-48% vs 113.9% KO risk on Basculegion). Charizard-Y is 80-120% OHKO risk from Lycanroc Rock (priority Accelerock guarantees first), second Protect is ~33% so switch preserves Drought for Froslass-Mega Snow Warning and saves Charizard. Whimsicott 184 Prankster Tailwind + Sash preserved better than Basculegion and sets Tailwind next vs 154-189 Froslass/ Chlorophyll Scovillain. Garchomp Protect would waste SunnyDay turn with no progress on 2x EQ targets.
Sneasler dies to EQ if it stays and Prankster Encore would lock last-turn Protect (1/3); switch Bascu who lives EQ/DC. Lycanroc Accelerock priority-KOs 21% Whimsicott then is expendable.
decisions.notebook: G1 mega Froslass only. Delay mega until after any Charizard-Y Drought so Snow overwrites. Sneasler Fake Out spent; Unburden still via CC+White Herb. Lycanroc sash already gone; TC Accelerock is the Charizard answer (4x, not a guaranteed OHKO). Froslass Blizzard 4x Garchomp; Heat Wave OHKOs Froslass even through Veil. decisions.notebook: G1 mega Froslass only. Delay mega until after any Charizard-Y Drought so Snow overwrites. Sneasler Fake Out spent G1; Unburden still via CC+White Herb. decisions.rationale: EQ super-effective 95-191% KO on Sneasler at 87% (spread 0.75x) and 94-187% on Lycanroc 1%, while Whimsicott Protect (Prankster +4) blocks ally EQ 34-41% KO and opponent Fake Out/Dire Claw 210% and Accelerock 30-46% KO. Rock Slide only 11-24% to Sneasler, Dragon Claw 51-103% not guaranteed. Protect preserves 21% Whimsicott for next-turn Prankster Tailwind/Encore vs Veil/SD; EQ applies max pressure even if Lycanroc protects (100%) and forces Sneasler to gamble second Protect at 50%.
