decisions.rationale: Garchomp Protect avoids guaranteed KO from Froslass 4x Blizzard (97-149%) and Basculegion Last Respects (67-98% at +1 faint). Whimsicott Tailwind is Prankster +1 and guaranteed first vs Froslass (184 vs 143-178) and Basculegion Aqua Jet (+1) on speed, securing Tailwind before spread Blizzard KOs the 21% Whimsicott (sash dead below 100%). Tailwind sac is optimal: Whimsicott at 21% has no sash value and Encore fails vs fresh entrants with no last move. Sac sets speed control (Garchomp 169*2, Charizard 125*2 outspeed Froslass-Mega 154-189) and preserves Garchomp at 64% for next turn Charizard-Mega-Y switch to overwrite Snow after Froslass mega.

Basculegion resists Blizzard (17-37% vs 41-57% into Charizard) and resists/is NVE to Wave Crash (Charizard is OHKO 144-215% before Sun, 72-107% after), survives Snow, is immune to Sneasler Fake Out/Close Combat, and threatens OHKO on Froslass (88-215% Last Respects) and enemy Basculegion 45% (EQ 37-71% + adapted Ghost), while keeping Tailwind speed advantage (236 vs 154-189). Charizard sun would deny Veil but dies to Adaptability Life Orb Wave Crash.
They outspeed and Last Respects OHKOes Froslass while Dragon Claw OHKOes Bascu; Protect saves Froslass and Aqua Jet is the only Bascu hit before it dies. Chip Garchomp (23-41%) over their full Bascu.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Garchomp Dragon Claw into Froslass-Mega (100% acc, 33-65%) + own Basculegion Last Respects into opp Basculegion 45% (102-192% guaranteed KO at 45% before it acts due to Tailwind speed 236 vs 98-130) - guarantees opp Basculegion removed before its Wave Crash (80-117% vs Garchomp 64%) can KO, chips Froslass to 35-67% so it is in KO range next turn under Tailwind. Rock Slide 90% acc risks miss leaving Froslass 15% alive; Dragon Claw better. Switching Garchomp to Charizard risks guaranteed OHKO Wave Crash 144-215% vs Charizard before our KO if opp uses Aqua Jet priority 48-73% + Blizzard 30-42% and leaves Froslass at 100%. Staying sacrifices Garchomp to Blizzard 151-216% but preserves Charizard at 100% for next turn and keeps Bascul egion healthy (only 12-28% from Blizzard) - best expected value with Protect-resilient split.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out Garchomp to flinch EQ/Dragon Claw or punish a Charizard switch; Froslass Protect is the only answer to Adaptability Last Respects (guaranteed OHKO) even at 33%.

Switch Garchomp 27% 4x weak to Blizzard into Charizard-Y to overwrite Snow with Drought (walls Blizzard, denies Veil and Ice Def boost, Tailwind still 2). Basculegion Wave Crash vs Sneasler 93-184% guaranteed KO from 87% before it can Close Combat/Bullet; EQ line would self-damage 52-62% and be hard punished by protects (Froslass protect 50% after last turn). Selected line guarantees one KO unless Sneasler protects, preserves momentum and weather control for next turn vs Froslass.
Sneasler Protects to live Aqua Jet/Heat Wave; Froslass Shadow Balls Basculegion, the only line that can KO Bascu if Heat Wave misses and then both can target Charizard after Tailwind.

Weather Ball Fire 100 BP guaranteed OHKO Froslass (125-229%) and Aqua Jet guaranteed KO Sneasler at 7% (15-31% >7%); both moves 100% accuracy vs Heat Wave 90%. Tailwind 250/236 outspeeds 154-189/140-172 so both KOs occur before foe moves if no Protect; split targets ensures Sneasler dies before it can act (preventing DireClaw/CloseCombat) while Froslass dies before ShadowBall/Blizzard. If Froslass Protects (streak 2 low chance) it uses its turn to Protect and Sneasler still dies to Aqua Jet for 2v1 next turn; double Protect low due to streak. Priority Aqua Jet also guarantees Sneasler KO next turn after Tailwind expires.
Game is unwinnable at 8% Sneasler vs two attackers; Aqua Jet KOs before I move if they priority, otherwise Dire Claw is the highest-roll chip plus Dire Claw status into Charizard.

Lycanroc Sash was burned by Garchomp Life Orb EQ while Charizard-Y Protected T1 then pivoted to Prankster Tailwind Whimsicott; Froslass mega KO'd Cott but Drought returned and Weather Ball OHKO'd it, after which Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion cleaned with Last Respects then Aqua Jet.
reflections.adjustment: Do not hard-commit Froslass mega into Charizard-Y sun. If they bring Zard+Chomp again, sit Froslass and/or Lycanroc; prefer Kingambit or Scovillain. Keep Sneasler Fake Out. If Zard sits, lead Froslass and mega T1.

Sneasler Unburden White Herb; Fake Out only on the first turn after each switch-in. Ground hits Ghost 1x.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott Tailwind is Prankster +1 priority, guaranteed before Sneasler/Scovillain 0-priority moves so Tailwind sets even if Whimsicott later KOed via sash; Garchomp at 27% is guaranteed KO by Sneasler Close Combat 52-75% so must Protect (100% success, last used T2) or switch, Protect preserves it and keeps Charizard at 100% in back away from Basculegion Wave Crash 144% OHKO, avoids Garchomp Earthquake ally chip 34-40% that would break Whimsicott sash and make Dire Claw 210% lethal, while Rock Slide insufficient vs Sneasler. Preserve Tailwind window to outspeed Scovillain 190-254 +2 next turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

EQ+Mega Heat Wave KOs Sneasler and likely Scovillain; Protect saves Sneasler while Scovillain stays in to Spicy Spray-burn Garchomp. Rage Powder is +2 and redirects any singles. Scovillain is -4 SpA and expendable.
decisions.notebook: Opp 6: Chomp Jolly LO RoughSkin Spe<=169 (Sneasler 172 outspeeds), Gambit Adamant Chople Defiant no Protect, Cott Prankster Sash Timid 149-184, Zard-Y Modest CharizarditeY, Bascu Mystic Water Adapt Spe<119, Floette-Eternal. G1-2 Chomp/Zard-Y/Cott/Bascu. G3 brought Chomp/Gambit/Cott/Zard-Y. Mega Scov used (Spicy Spray burns any attacker that hits it). Sneasler Unburden White Herb; Fake Out only first turn after each switch-in. Ground hits Ghost 1x. Bascu Aqua Jet/Wave Crash threaten Zard without sun; Lycanroc Accelerock 4x Zard with priority. Do not consecutive-Protect blindly; burn Chomp then bring Bascu.

decisions.rationale: Send Basculegion to tank sun-boosted Fire (Heat Wave/Weather Ball leave it healthy) while Wave Crash/Last Respects threaten the KO on Zard; burned 11% Chomp dies to almost any hit or its own LO+burn if it attacks. Lycanroc is -1 Def/SpD, sash inactive, and loses the double.

Tailwind 338/250 vs 190-254/140-172 lets both ours move first. Garchomp EQ is spread 95.7-191% guaranteed OHKO vs Sneasler (87%) before Sneasler CloseCombat 52-75% can KO Garchomp (27%), bypasses Rage Powder (spread not redirected) and Protect only blocks Sneasler. EQ also does 38.4-73.6% to Scovillain-Mega (-4 SpA does 9-14% back, not lethal). Charizard Heat Wave spread 36.6-69.3% to Scovillain + EQ = 75-143% now, with Mega-Y Drought before priority moves sun 1.5x => ~54-103% to Scovillain and halves Basculegion Aqua Jet 48-73%->24-36% / WaveCrash if they switch Sneasler->Basculegion (EQ 37.9-71.8% to Basculegion). Heat Wave spread also bypasses Rage Powder. Mega this turn sets sun before Aqua Jet/Accelerock priority. Garchomp Protect is 50% after last turn and unnecessary.
Wave Crash KOs Zard on any real Modest spread even in sun; switching Sneasler preserves it on the bench while Lycanroc takes the Fire hit and enables Accelerock if Zard Protects.
Only Sneasler remains; send it in vs 3% Zard-Y to take the game.

Weather Ball->Sneasler + EQ maximizes Sneasler removal. Guarantees KO if EQ resolves (69-128 + 48-95 >87) and still 69% KO if Basculegion Aqua-Jets Garchomp before EQ (priority +1 vs 0), leaving Charizard facing only Basculegion Wave Crash 71-108 (21% OHKO) instead of guaranteed DireClaw+WaveCrash KO. Keeps pressure on Tailwind turn and retains Garchomp if Sneasler dies before its DireClaw.
Fake Out KOs 3% Zard before Tailwind Heat Wave/Weather Ball, which both OHKO Sneasler; Protect stall also wins next turn after Tailwind ends (172>120-152) but Fake Out wins on the attack.

Tailwind last turn gives Charizard 250 vs 140-172 so we act first vs 0-priority Dire Claw/Close Combat. Weather Ball in Sun is 100BP Fire 69-128% vs Sneasler 87% - highest min and 100% acc vs Heat Wave 64.7-121.9% 90% acc, Ancient Power 9-17% cannot KO. Any hit KOs our 3% HP, and after Tailwind we are slower and lose. Protect vs any Sneasler move only wastes Tailwind and we still lose next turn to faster KO, so Protect EV 0%. Weather Ball maximizes P(KO before Sneasler attacks) if opponent attacks, while Fake Out/Protect by opponent beats us anyway. Target foe1 Sneasler.

reflections.summary: Won G3 and the series 2-1. Fake Out plus Close Combat created the early damage lead; Mega Scovillain Overheat KO'd Kingambit, then Overheat plus Dire Claw removed Whimsicott; Spicy Spray burn plus residual KO'd Garchomp, and Wave Crash left Mega Charizard on chip for a re-entry Fake Out finish. The between-game Mega Scovillain bring and burn-then-Basculegion plan helped; 0 errors. Encored Protect on Lycanroc only stalled one turn.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Sneasler Fake Out cycling, Mega Scovillain redirect/burn/Overheat, and Basculegion as the recoil Water nuke. Stop consecutive Protect. Re-pick the four each round; Froslass Veil and Kingambit are still unused tools.
reflections.notebook: Sneasler Fake Out only on the first turn after each switch-in; re-enter to reuse it. White Herb clears the first stat drop then Unburden doubles Speed. Mega Scovillain Spicy Spray burns whoever hits it; Rage Powder redirects; Overheat is the KO button; Moody can spike Speed before mega. Pair Rage Powder with partner Protect. Ground hits Ghost 1x. Do not consecutive-Protect. Basculegion Life Orb plus Wave Crash recoil can self-KO; Aqua Jet for priority; Last Respects scales after allies faint. Lycanroc Sash buys one action. Froslass mega Snow enables Aurora Veil. Kingambit Sucker Punch fails unless the target chose a damaging move.

reflections.summary: Lost Game 3 in 9 turns to be eliminated 1-2 in the quarterfinal; leading 3% Charizard-Mega-Y + 1 turn of Tailwind/Sun vs 87% Sneasler, Charizard was KO'd by Sneasler's Fake Out on the final turn.
reflections.notebook: Series 1-1. Opp top8 roster confirmed: Scovillain Grass/Fire Scovillainite Moody->Spicy Spray (burn attacker on hit) Bold Overheat/GigaDrain/Rage Powder/Protect, Moody +2 Spe -1 Def T1; Rage Powder powder fails vs Grass Whimsicott/Overcoat. Basculegion Adamant LifeOrb Adaptability WaveCrash/Last Respects/Aqua Jet/Protect Last Respects scales 50+50 per faint, Aqua Jet picks low HP CharY. Sneasler Adamant WhiteHerb Unburden FakeOut/CloseCombat/DireClaw/Protect. Lycanroc-Dusk Adamant FocusSash ToughClaws Accelerock/CloseCombat/RockSlide/Protect priority threatens CharY. Froslass-Mega and Kingambit BlackGlasses SwordsDance not brought G2 but seen G1. Tendency: switches Scovillain into EQ to burn physical, heavy double Protect + switches to waste Tailwind/Sun, conserves Basculegion for Last Respects sweep. Our validated: Garchomp Jolly LifeOrb 169 EQ spread KOs Sneasler, Whimsicott Timid 184 Prankster Sash Tailwind beats initial Moody, Basculegion Adamant MysticWater Adapt loses mirror to LO when burned. Plan G3: keep EQ pressure but avoid early physical contact with Scovillain-Mega, maximize Tailwind damage window, protect Charizard health, bring Ghost resist (Kingambit Sucker Punch) or keep Basculegion unburned with Protect for Last Respects exchange.

retrospective.didWell: Recovered well after turn 1 Fake Out + Close Combat left Garchomp at 27% by using Protect + Tailwind on turn 2 and Encore on Lycanroc's Protect on turn 3 to deny momentum. Re-established Tailwind on turn 6 while protecting the burned Garchomp and transitioned cleanly to Mega Charizard-Y on turn 7 for sun. Turn 7-8 sequencing was strong: Rage Powder-immune Earthquake + Heat Wave removed Mega Scovillain through Sneasler's Protect, then Earthquake next turn KO'd Lycanroc-Dusk and left Basculegion in Weather Ball + Wave Crash recoil range.
retrospective.didPoorly: Kingambit’s Sucker Punch on turn 5 failed into Scovillain/Sneasler and left it to take a free super-effective Overheat for no trade while Tailwind expired. Recycled the 27% Garchomp back in on turn 6 where Mega Scovillain’s Spicy Spray burn plus Life Orb and burn chip guaranteed it died to residual before it could contribute beyond two Earthquakes. Left Whimsicott exposed to Overheat + Dire Claw on turn 6 after its Sash was broken, and finished with Charizard at 3% with no Protect against a fresh Sneasler with Fake Out available despite having Tailwind.
retrospective.wouldChange: On turn 5 with Scovillain at -2 and Sneasler just in, use Kowtow Cleave / Iron Head instead of Sucker Punch that had no priority target. Avoid re-entering 27% Garchomp on turn 6 into Mega Scovillain; keep Kingambit or bring Charizard a turn earlier to preserve a healthy ground immunity. On turn 9 with Tailwind still active and Sneasler as last opponent, Protect the 3% Charizard to waste Fake Out and force a 50/50 next turn instead of passing.

decisions.rationale: Floette and Basculegion jointly pressure Aerodactyl, Garchomp, Charizard, and Farigiraf leads; Choice Scarf Garchomp supplies fast Rock/Ground coverage, while Kingambit provides the best defensive and Trick Room insurance.

Their team is priority- and physical-heavy (Sneasler Fake Out/Feint, Kingambit Sucker Punch, Basculegion Aqua Jet, Dragonite Extreme Speed), so Farigiraf's Armor Tail is a huge back-line trump, and Mega Aerodactyl (187+ Speed) outruns Sneasler/Floette-Mega/scarf Garchomp while offering Tailwind and spread Rock Slide. Sylveon leads as a bulky Fairy that resists Dark/Fighting/Fairy and spreads Pixilate Hyper Voice into Dragonite, Garchomp and Sneasler. Kingambit is the dedicated answer to Basculegion (0.5x Last Respects, 2x Sucker Punch) and Floette-Mega (Iron Head). Charizard is left home because opposing Choice Scarf Garchomp's Rock Slide is 4x on it, and I only get one Mega anyway.
decisions.notebook:
MEGA PLAN: use Aerodactylite (Mega Aero: Tough Claws, raw Spe ~187+, outspeeds Sneasler 154-189, Floette-Mega 109-169, scarf Garchomp 122-154). Charizard-Y is a trap vs their scarf Garchomp Rock Slide (4x) - only bring if their Garchomp is gone/irrelevant.
OPPONENT KEY FACTS: Floette-Eternal + Floettite -> Floette-Mega, Fairy Aura, base SpA 155/SpD 148/Spe 102; Fairy Aura boosts BOTH sides' Fairy moves, so my Sylveon Hyper Voice also gets 1.33x while it is out. Floette is weak to Steel/Poison -> Kingambit Iron Head. Sylveon resists Fairy and is the best Light of Ruin sponge.
Their priority suite: Sneasler Fake Out/Feint, Kingambit Sucker Punch, Basculegion Aqua Jet, Dragonite Extreme Speed - ALL nullified by Farigiraf's Armor Tail (protects ally too). Farigiraf Psychic is 4x on Sneasler.
Basculegion: Adaptability + Life Orb Last Respects scales with their fainted count - avoid giving up KOs early; Kingambit takes Ghost at 0.5x and Sucker Punches back for 2x.
GAME 1 PLAN: lead Sylveon + Aerodactyl (double spread offense, mega Aero turn 1, Tailwind if the speed race needs it), back Farigiraf + Kingambit for late-game priority denial and Basculegion/Floette control.

decisions.rationale: Mega Dazzling Gleam plus priority Aqua Jet pressures both foes and reliably focuses Aerodactyl while giving Aqua Jet a chance to remove it before it can act.

Basculegion's Adaptability + Life Orb Wave Crash is a guaranteed OHKO on Aerodactyl (199-293%), and a Mega Floette Light of Ruin would likely finish it too, so keeping Aero in (let alone spending the Mega) throws my Mega away for ~20-40% chip. I pivot Aero out to Farigiraf, which survives either single attack (Wave Crash 61-90%, LoR 50-71%), shuts off their whole priority suite with Armor Tail, and sets up the Trick Room plan my slow core wants. Sylveon fires Hyper Voice for guaranteed chip on both (28-49% / 32-59%) since it survives anything single-target this turn.
decisions.notebook:
CORRECTION: Fairy does NOT resist Fairy - Sylveon takes Light of Ruin at 1x (41-61%). Basculegion (Adaptability+Life Orb) Wave Crash: OHKOs Aerodactyl (199-293%), 80-118% on Sylveon (roll KO), 61-90% on Farigiraf, so Basculegion is their #1 threat; it takes 33% recoil each Wave Crash.
MEGA PLAN REVISED: Aerodactyl is nearly unusable vs this team (Wave Crash/Aqua Jet 2x, Garchomp Rock Slide 2x, Mega Floette LoR ~KO). Hold the Mega; only Mega Aero if Basculegion and Garchomp are gone. Default win route = Farigiraf Trick Room, then Sylveon (80) and Kingambit (102) move first under TR.
DAMAGE REFS (turn-1 board): Sylveon Hyper Voice spread 28-49% on Floette, 32-59% on Basculegion; Aero Rock Slide 20-40% Floette, 16-31% Basculegion.
OPPONENT: Floette-Eternal + Floettite -> Mega (Fairy Aura, boosts BOTH sides' Fairy moves incl. my Hyper Voice). Floette is weak to Steel/Poison -> Kingambit Iron Head is my main answer. Their priority suite (Sneasler Fake Out/Feint, Kingambit Sucker Punch, Basculegion Aqua Jet, Dragonite Extreme Speed) is all blocked by Farigiraf's Armor Tail, which also protects the ally. Basculegion Last Respects scales with THEIR fainted count - don't hand out early KOs. Farigiraf Psychic is 4x on Sneasler. My Kingambit has Focus Sash (guaranteed one survival).
GAME PLAN: keep Farigiraf alive as the TR/priority-denial pivot, use Sylveon spread chip, save Kingambit to remove Floette and to trade with Basculegion (Ghost 0.5x into Kingambit).

decisions.rationale: Moonblast guarantees the Farigiraf KO, while Wave Crash guarantees the Sylveon KO if Basculegion is not removed by Quick Attack; splitting targets maximizes immediate knockout pressure.
Bring in Choice Scarf Garchomp to pressure the returning Aerodactyl immediately while preserving Kingambit for the endgame.

Both foes outspeed and OHKO both of my actives, so I can only protect one and swing with the other. Farigiraf (Armor Tail priority blank + Trick Room) is the piece I must keep and is the likeliest target, so it Protects. Sylveon's Hyper Beam is a guaranteed KO on Mega Floette from 47% (74.6-126.8%), removing their Mega and biggest threat; the recharge is acceptable since Sylveon is already in OHKO range of everything. Hyper Voice would only guarantee the KO on a 24% Basculegion that self-destructs with Wave Crash recoil + Life Orb anyway.
decisions.notebook:
CORRECTION: Fairy does NOT resist Fairy - Sylveon takes Light of Ruin at 1x. Fairy Aura (their Mega Floette) boosts BOTH sides' Fairy moves, including my Pixilate Hyper Voice/Hyper Beam/Quick Attack.
KEY DAMAGE (this board): Sylveon HV spread 41-77% Basculegion, 33-57% Floette-Mega; Sylveon Hyper Beam 75-127% into Floette-Mega (single-target nuke, 90% acc, recharge turn); Sylveon Quick Attack only 13-25% (physical, Atk 76 - avoid). Farigiraf Thunderbolt 31-57% on Basculegion (2x); Farigiraf Psychic only 18-32% on Floette. Foe LoR: guaranteed OHKO on my Sylveon and Farigiraf at current chip; Moonblast 46-64% Sylveon; Basculegion Wave Crash OHKOs Sylveon/Farigiraf/Aerodactyl; Last Respects 34-50% on Sylveon and 0x on Farigiraf.
Basculegion at low HP self-KOs with Wave Crash (1/3 recoil + Life Orb 10%). Don't waste resources killing it; make it kill itself.
SPEED PROBLEM: Sylveon and Farigiraf are both 80, slower than Floette (134-169) and Basculegion (98-130). Trick Room is the only way to move first; Farigiraf must survive the turn it casts (TR is -7). Protect Farigiraf when both foes can KO it.
MEGA PLAN: Aerodactyl is nearly unusable vs Wave Crash/Aqua Jet/Garchomp Rock Slide; hold the Mega unless Basculegion and Garchomp are gone.
KINGAMBIT (mine, Focus Sash, Adamant, 102 Spe): main answer to Floette (Iron Head SE), resists Ghost, neutral to Fairy; save it as the closer, and don't let it eat two hits in one turn (Sash only saves once).
Their priority core (Sneasler Fake Out/Feint, Kingambit Sucker Punch, Dragonite Extreme Speed, Basculegion Aqua Jet) is fully blanked by Farigiraf's Armor Tail, which also covers the ally - keeping Farigiraf alive is worth a lot.
Unknown remaining foes: 2 of {Kingambit(Chople), Dragonite(Mega stone, Multiscale), Garchomp(Choice Scarf), Sneasler(Sash)}. Farigiraf Psychic is 4x on Sneasler.

decisions.rationale: Sylveon fainted; Kingambit is the correct replacement. Light of Ruin OHKOs Aerodactyl outright, while Kingambit is only 1x to Fairy and holds Focus Sash, so it always lives a hit and its Iron Head is a guaranteed KO on Floette-Mega at 47%. Kingambit also pairs with Farigiraf's Armor Tail (blanks their Sucker Punch/Extreme Speed/Fake Out/Aqua Jet priority) and benefits from Trick Room if Farigiraf gets it up. Aerodactyl's Mega is held in reserve until Garchomp is accounted for.
decisions.notebook:
CORRECTION: Fairy does NOT resist Fairy. Fairy Aura (their Mega Floette) boosts BOTH sides' Fairy moves.
DEAD: my Sylveon; their Basculegion (self-KO'd via Wave Crash recoil+Life Orb).
MY REMAINING: Farigiraf (Sitrus, Armor Tail, Bold, 80 Spe; Psychic/Thunderbolt/Trick Room/Protect), Kingambit (Focus Sash, Defiant, Adamant, 102 Spe), Aerodactyl (Aerodactylite, Jolly, 183 Spe / Mega 187-222).
THEIR REMAINING: Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura, Timid, 134-169 Spe, Moonblast/Dazzling Gleam/Light of Ruin/Protect) plus 2 unknown of {Kingambit(Chople), Dragonite(Mega stone, Multiscale), Garchomp(Choice Scarf), Sneasler(Sash)} - they already Mega'd Floette, so their Dragonite cannot Mega.
KEY DAMAGE: My Kingambit Iron Head 2x on Floette = KO from ~47%; Floette Light of Ruin into Kingambit 65-139% (Sash saves once); LoR guaranteed OHKO on Aerodactyl and on chipped Farigiraf; Aerodactyl Rock Slide only 23-43% on Floette.
PLANS: Kingambit is the closer - Iron Head for Floette/Sneasler(? Steel neutral) and Fairy foes, Sucker Punch for KO'd-out finishing, Low Kick vs their Kingambit. Don't let Kingambit eat two attacks in one turn (Sash saves once). Farigiraf's Armor Tail blanks all their priority for both slots - keeping it alive is high value; Trick Room (-7) makes Kingambit 102 move before Floette. Farigiraf Psychic is 4x on Sneasler. Hold Aerodactyl's Mega unless Garchomp (Scarf Rock Slide) is confirmed absent/dead; Mega Aero outspeeds their whole team including Sneasler.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Kingambit with Stomping Tantrum followed by Moonblast, guaranteeing the KO before it can threaten Floette while denying Focus Sash.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Kingambit)

reflections.summary: You won game 2 and the series 2-0 by converting immediate offensive pressure into favorable trades. Dazzling Gleam plus Wave Crash secured the first knockout, switching Basculegion out preserved it for the endgame, and Kingambit absorbed pressure before Low Kick removed the opposing Kingambit. The final split targeting let Basculegion and Kingambit eliminate both remaining targets. The Dual Wingbeat miss reduced endgame risk, so favorable variance contributed, but the positioning and target selection created the winning line. The between-game adaptations helped: you respected priority denial, focused down Kingambit, and preserved your own Kingambit rather than relying on blocked priority.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the proactive Floette–Basculegion pressure and the willingness to pivot Basculegion away from unfavorable board states. Continue using Kingambit as a durable midgame pivot and finisher. Do not make major changes after a clean, error-free win, but account for Wave Crash recoil plus Life Orb damage when deciding whether Basculegion should attack, Protect, or switch. Against unfamiliar teams, reassess priority control, speed control, and likely Protects rather than carrying over opponent-specific reads.
reflections.notebook: Use Floette’s spread pressure to soften both slots while a partner concentrates damage for knockouts. Mega Floette can force defensive turns, but avoid committing its strongest single-target attack when Protect is strongly telegraphed. Preserve Life Orb Basculegion when recoil would compromise its ability to clean later; Aqua Jet is only a plan when priority is permitted. Kingambit is valuable as both a defensive pivot and late-game attacker, with Low Kick providing important coverage into heavy targets. Keep Sneasler available as a fast closer offering Fake Out, Feint, Focus Sash, and broad physical pressure. At preview, identify priority denial, speed-control modes, and which attacker best fits the matchup; consider Scarf Garchomp or a Mega Dragonite mode when immediate speed or different coverage is more valuable than Mega Floette.

retrospective.didWell: Turn 2's Protect on Farigiraf was clean value, eating a Light of Ruin for nothing and keeping Armor Tail on the field so their Sucker Punch/Aqua Jet lines were shut off. Turn 3 I picked the right target and move with Kingambit, Iron Head KOing Mega Floette-Eternal before it could snowball, and turn 4 Farigiraf's Thunderbolt was the correct super-effective click to remove Life Orb Adaptability Basculegion. Across four turns I traded down their mega, their Kingambit and their Basculegion, so the individual KO reads were mostly sound even as the position collapsed.
retrospective.didPoorly: The lead was the game-loser: Sylveon at 80 Speed was put in front of Adaptability Life Orb Basculegion and died to Wave Crash before ever moving, while I simultaneously pivoted Aerodactyl out, so turn 1 cost me a Pokémon for zero damage. Turn 2 I clicked Kowtow Cleave into their Dark/Steel Kingambit (resisted, 81%) when Low Kick was 4x and would have KO'd immediately, which is the same button I correctly found one turn too late. I also brought Trick Room on an 80/80/102-Speed squad and never used it, double-Protecting with Farigiraf on turns 2 and 3 instead, and on turn 4 I clicked Dual Wingbeat into Basculegion, a 90%-accurate neutral move that could not KO even on a hit, while Rock Slide's spread flinch chance was the only line that kept Farigiraf alive.
retrospective.wouldChange: Lead Aerodactyl + Farigiraf and keep Sylveon in the back, since Sylveon is outsped and one-shot by their Basculegion and contributes nothing from the lead slot. On turn 2, click Low Kick rather than Kowtow Cleave into their Kingambit for the immediate 4x KO, leaving Floette alone in a 2v1. Use Trick Room with Farigiraf on turn 2 instead of the second Protect, since the squad I brought only functions under it. On turn 4, click Rock Slide with Mega Aerodactyl to hit both and roll for a flinch on Kingambit rather than a Dual Wingbeat that cannot KO Basculegion even when it connects.

decisions.rationale: Lead Froslass and Sneasler for immediate Fake Out control and Mega Snow Warning Blizzard/Aurora Veil pressure, with Basculegion and Kingambit in the back as powerful priority cleaners.
decisions.notebook:
Game 1 vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Floette-Eternal/Dragonite/Sneasler/Kingambit.
Opponent team details:
- Whimsicott @ Focus Sash, Prankster (Moonblast, Tailwind, Encore, Protect)
- Basculegion @ Life Orb, Adaptability (Wave Crash, Last Respects, Aqua Jet, Protect)
- Floette-Eternal @ Floettite, Flower Veil (Moonblast, Dazzling Gleam, Light of Ruin, Protect)
- Dragonite @ Dragoninite, Multiscale on Mega (Dragon Pulse, Heat Wave, Thunderbolt, Protect)
- Sneasler @ White Herb, Unburden (Dire Claw, Close Combat, Rock Slide, Fake Out)
- Kingambit @ Chople Berry, Defiant (Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, Low Kick, Sucker Punch)
Our plan: Lead Froslass (Mega) + Sneasler for Fake Out + Snow Warning Blizzard / Aurora Veil setup, with Basculegion and Kingambit to clean up.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind and Sneasler for fast Fake Out/Rock Slide pressure; keep Adaptability Basculegion and Mega Floette-Eternal in back for late-game Water/Ghost and Fairy Aura offense.

Sneasler uses Fake Out (+3 priority) on Whimsicott to break its Focus Sash and flinch it before Prankster Tailwind (+1 priority) can activate. Froslass Mega Evolves to trigger Snow Warning and fires off a 100% accurate Blizzard to eliminate Whimsicott turn 1 and chunk foe Sneasler.
Prankster Tailwind secures speed control; Sneasler's faster Fake Out flinches the opposing Sneasler before it can Fake Out Whimsicott.

Blizzard in Snowscape is 100% accurate and spread-damage calculations guarantee KOs on both 1% HP Whimsicott and 38% HP Sneasler. Sneasler targets foe Sneasler with Close Combat to guarantee the KO if Rock Slide flinches Froslass.

Whimsicott's Encore is Normal and Froslass-Mega is Ghost, so Encore fails. Moonblast + Rock Slide both pressure Froslass before it can move; the combined chip puts Froslass in range for Basculegion next turn even if Aurora Veil goes up, and Rock Slide has a flinch chance to stop Aurora Veil/Blizzard.

Send Floette-Eternal into Whimsicott's slot opposite Froslass-Mega and Basculegion into Sneasler's slot opposite the opposing Sneasler; this gives the more favorable defensive matchups while both are faster under Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal holds Floettite and Mega Evolves into Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura). Basculegion's Last Respects gains 50 BP per fainted ally. Prefer Floette opposite Froslass-Mega and Basculegion opposite Sneasler.

decisions.rationale: Opponent has 2 turns of Tailwind remaining with Floette-Eternal and Basculegion on the field. Neither foe has setup moves, status moves, or Protect-bypassing abilities/moves. Double Protect stalls a turn of Tailwind with 100% reliability, keeping Kingambit and Basculegion fresh on the bench.

Mega Evolve Floette to get Fairy Aura and enough power for Moonblast to guaranteed KO Sneasler from 59%, while Basculegion's priority Aqua Jet guaranteed KOs Froslass-Mega from 23% before it can move. This covers Protect mindgames: whichever target does not Protect is removed before attacking, and both attacks are 100% accurate.

Tailwind is on its final turn while our backline of full-HP Basculegion and Kingambit is pristine. Staying in to attack with Blizzard and Gunk Shot punishes any split targeting or Protect from the opponent and ensures our backline enters cleanly on turn 5 when Tailwind expires.
Bring out our remaining two Pokémon: Basculegion in slot 1 and Kingambit in slot 2.

Floette-Mega outspeeds and Moonblast is a guaranteed KO on Froslass-Mega from 23%, preventing Aurora Veil or Blizzard. Basculegion's 150 BP Last Respects is a guaranteed KO on Sneasler from 59% and avoids Wave Crash recoil, preserving Basculegion's HP. This keeps Floette opposite Froslass and Basculegion opposite Sneasler, the safer alignment.

Kingambit's Sucker Punch has +1 priority, moving before foe Basculegion's standard attacks (Wave Crash / Last Respects) and guaranteeing an OHKO (116.8-138.1%). Basculegion targets Floette-Mega with 150 BP Adaptability Life Orb Last Respects (96.1-179.9%), covering both opposing slots for a decisive double knockout or clean endgame.
Protect Basculegion to blank the expected double-target, while Floette's Moonblast chunks the opposing Basculegion so Floette can finish it next turn before it moves.

Both our faster Basculegion with Last Respects and Kingambit with Kowtow Cleave deal well over 100% to opponent's remaining Basculegion. Targeting foe 2 with both guarantees the Game 1 win regardless of priority or consecutive Protect.

Floette is fainted, so pass. Wave Crash into Kingambit is the only move with a possible OHKO and a real path to win if the 7% Basculegion protects or uses Aqua Jet; Aqua Jet into Basculegion would still leave us KOed by Kingambit after Life Orb recoil.

reflections.summary: Mega Froslass's Blizzard severely punished the opponent's Whimsicott and Sneasler lead. Double Protect on Turn 3 stalled the final turns of Tailwind, allowing our Jolly Basculegion to outspeed and eliminate both Mega Floette and their Adamant Basculegion.
reflections.adjustment: Maintain the strong Froslass + Sneasler lead into Kingambit + Basculegion backline, but be alert if the opponent adjusts by leading Kingambit (Chople Berry) or Dragonite to counter Blizzard.
reflections.notebook:
Opponent tendencies and strategic facts:
- Opponent Basculegion is Adamant (Speed <= 130); our Jolly Basculegion (Speed 143) naturally outspeeds and OHKOs with Last Respects outside Tailwind.
- Opponent Sneasler is Jolly and outspeeds our Adamant Sneasler on Fake Out turns.
- Opponent Floette-Eternal runs Floettite (Mega with Fairy Aura).
- Opponent Game 1 selection was Whimsicott / Sneasler / Floette / Basculegion (did not bring Chople Kingambit or Dragonite).
- Double Protect successfully burned opponent's Tailwind turns.

reflections.summary: We lost because the opponent's late-game Adaptability Basculegion swept with boosted Last Respects. After Whimsicott and Sneasler fell to Froslass's turn-2 Blizzard, Floette and Basculegion evened the game, but on turn 5 Basculegion Protected to avoid Kingambit's Sucker Punch, which failed; Floette's Moonblast only left the opposing Basculegion at 17%, and it OHKOed Floette. Our Basculegion then traded with theirs but died to Life Orb recoil, leaving full-health Kingambit as the winner.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, keep Floette for Froslass and preserve an offensive answer to the opponent's end-game Basculegion. Do not burn Basculegion's turn on Protect into Kingambit while the opposing Basculegion is active; attack it to prevent Last Respects. Consider Fake Out into Froslass to blunt Snow-boosted Blizzard and be ready for double Protect after our switch-ins.
reflections.notebook: Durable opponent notes: Leads Froslass-Mega + Sneasler; Mega Froslass sets Snow and attacks with Blizzard turn 1 rather than Aurora Veil. Opponent will double Protect to stall Tailwind or after our switch-ins. End-game Basculegion (Jolly, Adaptability, Life Orb) is the primary win condition: Last Respects becomes an OHKO threat after 2+ faints, and it may Protect when expecting Sucker Punch. Kingambit has Black Glasses and uses Sucker Punch to punish unprotected attackers. Future plan: keep Basculegion healthy enough to finish their Basculegion before it moves, and avoid relying on Protect to neutralize Sucker Punch while Basculegion is active.

Team Strategic Guidelines:

retrospective.didWell: Your turn 3 Rock Slide plus Kingambit pressure removed Mega Froslass, and the turn 2 Rock Slide flinch briefly disrupted the opponent. The turn 5 double Protect correctly stalled the opponent's attacks and blocked their boosted Last Respects. retrospective.didPoorly: Repeated Sucker Punch attempts into Froslass on turns 1-2 were ineffective because Froslass was Protecting or setting Aurora Veil, letting the opponent set Veil without pressure. retrospective.wouldChange: Pressure Froslass early with Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head or a defensive read instead of repeatedly clicking Sucker Punch, especially once Aurora Veil was the obvious turn-2 play. On turn 4, Protect Sneasler or hard swap it to Basculegion rather than attacking at 17%, to avoid losing it for free to Aqua Jet. On turn 6, use Encore or Moonblast with Whimsicott for final value instead of risking a consecutive Protect failure. In the 1v2, try to force a 1v1 by attacking the 54% Kingambit with priority rather than Protecting and leaving both opposing threats untouched.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott leads with Prankster Encore to punish Sneasler's Fake Out (lesson 2), giving Basculegion a protected free turn to start stacking damage toward Last Respects scaling; Kingambit backs up as a bulky secondary wincon that resists the opposing Rock/Normal attacks and punishes anything boosting, and Charizard-Y sits in back to Mega in against Ice/Ghost Froslass (Fire/Ancient Power both 2x) and to fight snow with Drought sun.
decisions.notebook: DURABLE TEAM LESSONS (fixed 6: Kingambit/Basculegion/Garchomp/Zard-Y/Whimsicott/Floette-E): (1) Last Respects + Adaptability Basculegion (Life Orb) is the win condition — BP scales with total faints, so time a late-game return: 150 BP at 5 faints vastly outdamaged even resisted Wave Crash into bulky resists (roughly 76-133% vs 31-54% in that matchup). Frontload faints are a resource, not a loss. (2) Whimsicott Encore is the anti-wall tool: Encore-locked onto a Protect-style move, the target's forced repeat fails outright when the consecutive-use streak breaks — that yields guaranteed free turns for a double-attack squeeze. Protect-streak itself: after a successful use, next use ~1/3; after a fail, next use is free. Encore on Sneasler turn 1 locks Fake Out, which auto-fails turn 2. (3) Zard-Y: Ancient Power beats Weather Ball/Heat Wave whenever weather is off — 60 BP 100% accurate, and it's the nuke vs Fire/Flying and Ice/Ghost targets (2x). Keep sun for Weather Ball turns only; Mega Froslass's Snow Warning will overwrite/conflict with Drought, so don't count on Weather Ball. (4) Toxic management: assume the counter softens on re-entry — a returning toxed mon buys extra clock; a toxed mon at ~13% is dead to the tick: spend it attacking, never on Protect. (5) Wide Guard only stops spread; protect-style stops only single-target attacks — combined single-target pressure is the universal answer to defensive shells. Watch Scovillain RagePowder redirection; Kingambit is immune-safe single-target pressure and DireClaw poison is the hazard to route around. (6) Defiant converts Intimidate into +2 Kingambit; opponent has no Intimidate on sheet, so Defiant is mostly idle here. (7) Encored attackers are predictable damage sinks — Encore-protect them and switch around their fixed target. (8) This foe's spread damage is Ice (Blizzard in snow) and Rock (Rock Slide) heavy; Lycanroc carries Focus Sash — chip twice or Encore-lock its attacks rather than fishing for the one-shot. These damage/matchup numbers were observed vs earlier series teams; recalibrate against new foes.

reflections.summary: Lost a 7-turn game that started with a winning trade but was thrown away in the midgame. Turn 1 was strong: Whimsicott's Protect blanked both Fake Out and Rock Slide, and Basculegion Wave Crashed Sneasler out — but Wave Crash recoil plus Life Orb left Basculegion at 30%, and the opponent's Focus Sash was never touched. Turn 3 was the pivotal blunder: switching Charizard-Y directly in front of the Encored Accelerock (2x) removed Zard from the game instantly without it ever acting. From there the tempo inverted — Tailwind re-clicked on turn 5 failed (already active), Whimsicott fell to Accelerock, and Low Kick was wasted into Ghost Froslass. Turn 6 their Lycanroc Close Combat (Tough Claws, 4x) removed Kingambit despite Occa Berry, and a 30% Basculegion 1v2 vs Froslass + Lycanroc could not front-run two +0 attackers — Accelerock ended it. Per endgame math, that 1v2 was unwinnable; the Charizard switch-in was what created it.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Whimsicott+Basculegion lead — the Protect-into-Fake-Out absorb plus an early KO on Sneasler is proven value against their Sneasler+Lycanroc lead. Fix the three leaks: (1) never switch a rock-weak frail mon into a known Encore lock — if Basculegion must vacate, bring Garchomp or Kingambit, not Charizard; (2) do not re-click Tailwind while it is active; (3) manage Basculegion's HP — recoil stacking on Wave Crash is what left it one Accelerock from dead; prefer Aqua Jet into Lycanroc (guaranteed OHKO per the -1 Def finding) when the sash-bearing lead is present. Expect Mega Froslass mid-game again: hold Kingambit away from Close Combat turns, and remember Low Kick does nothing to Froslass. Zard-Y's weather plan is threatened by Froslass's Mega Snow — bring it only with a plan to remove Froslass first (Last Respects is 2x into it).

retrospective.didWell: Turn 1 was excellent: I predicted both opponents would target Basculegion and Protected, fully blunting Lycanroc's Accelerock and Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The Turn 2 Encore locking Lycanroc into Accelerock bought several free turns, and the Turn 6 trade was favorable — sacrificing Whimsicott to remove Lycanroc and chip Froslass with Earthquake. Late-game, my Turn 8 Low Kick cleanly removed the +2 opposing Kingambit, and Turn 10 Last Respects traded my Kingambit for Sneasler to reach an even 1v1.
retrospective.didPoorly: Turn 8 I gambled on a consecutive Garchomp Protect, it failed, and the super-effective Blizzard removed Garchomp outright — the same turn a resisted crit also gutted Kingambit. Turn 10 I called Sucker Punch into Froslass, but it used Aurora Veil, so the attack failed for a full wasted action that let Sneasler's Close Combat kill my Kingambit. The decisive error was Turn 11: facing a 46% Froslass with a faster-than-expected opponent, I selected Last Respects instead of priority Aqua Jet, and Adaptability Life Orb Aqua Jet very plausibly KOs before Froslass's Shadow Ball lands.
retrospective.wouldChange: On Turn 11, click Aqua Jet with Basculegion — priority removes the speed question entirely against a 46% frail Froslass and likely wins the game. On Turn 8, don't chain Protect with Garchomp; attacking or switching preserves a key piece against Blizzard under Snow. On Turn 10, given Froslass had Protected twice already and could Veil, attack with Basculegion's stronger action rather than betting the slow Kingambit on Sucker Punch. Finally, watch Tailwind timing — my second Tailwind expired on Turn 9 right when the endgame arrived, so re-setting or protecting around its expiry deserves more attention.

reflections.summary: Won the series 2-0. Game 2 closed because Lycanroc Accelerock broke the Tailwind/Encore support, Mega Froslass Protect-mega into Blizzard removed Garchomp, Sneasler Close Combat removed Kingambit, and Shadow Ball cleaned Basculegion. The between-game plan (Sneasler into Kingambit, Mega Froslass as closer, Lycanroc sash pressure) helped; Kingambit Swords Dance behind Protect backfired when Low Kick fainted it unused, and parking Froslass on Earthquake cost Lycanroc plus half of Froslass.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Lycanroc sash pressure with Mega Froslass snow/Veil/Blizzard as the default closer and Sneasler as the Steel answer. Do not treat Kingambit Swords Dance as a converted wincon. Next list is new: swap Lycanroc or Kingambit for Basculegion or Scovillain if there is no frail support to chip or if redirect/Fire Mega is needed.
reflections.notebook: Lycanroc lead: Accelerock the support, then switch the instant Encore lands. Mega Froslass: Protect on the mega turn, then Aurora Veil or snow Blizzard; Shadow Ball covers Ghosts when Basculegion is benched. Never send Froslass into Earthquake. Sneasler Fake-Outs, Close Combats Steel, and Protects into Last Respects; White Herb exists to clear the CC drops. Kingambit Protect-into-Swords Dance only if it lives the next hit. Double Protect expires Tailwind and makes Sucker Punch fail. Default this four vs Tailwind+Steel; keep Basculegion and Scovillain for Ghost offense or Rage Powder/Fire Mega.

events.text: Aurora Veil up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Scarf Garchomp and Sneasler for immediate speed and physical pressure into Froslass, Sneasler, Lycanroc, and Kingambit. Preserve Mega Dragonite for broad special coverage and Kingambit as a durable late-game answer to Froslass, Basculegion, and opposing Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Use Floette’s spread pressure to soften both slots while a partner concentrates damage for knockouts. Mega Floette can force defensive turns, but avoid committing its strongest single-target attack when Protect is strongly telegraphed. Preserve Life Orb Basculegion when recoil would compromise its ability to clean later; Aqua Jet is only a plan when priority is permitted. Kingambit is valuable as both a defensive pivot and late-game attacker, with Low Kick providing important coverage into heavy targets. Keep Sneasler available as a fast closer offering Fake Out, Feint, Focus Sash, and broad physical pressure. At preview, identify priority denial, speed-control modes, and which attacker best fits the matchup; consider Scarf Garchomp or a Mega Dragonite mode when immediate speed or different coverage is more valuable than Mega Floette.

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Froslass and Sneasler for immediate Fake Out support and Snow/Blizzard/Aurora Veil pressure into Dragonite, Garchomp, and Floette, with Kingambit and Basculegion in the back to pivot defensively and clean up late game.
decisions.notebook:
Team Strategic Guidelines:
- Mega Froslass (Timid, Speed 189) provides Fake Out immunity, instant Snow Defense boost, fast Aurora Veil setup, and Blizzard spread damage/freeze threat.
- Sneasler (Adamant) triggers Unburden immediately upon consuming its White Herb after Close Combat, reaching high-speed offensive pressure with Fighting and Poison STABs.
- Basculegion (Jolly, Speed 143, Life Orb, Adaptability) is the primary late-game win condition; preserve it until teammates faint to maximize Last Respects power, using Aqua Jet for priority cleanup.
- Kingambit (Defiant, Black Glasses) provides vital defensive switching into Ghost- and Dark-type attacks aimed at Basculegion/Froslass, discouraging stat drops and offering Sucker Punch/Kowtow Cleave priority and power.
- When facing opposing Tailwind or speed control, utilize Protect cycling and Kingambit's resistances under Aurora Veil to stall out turns cleanly.
- Scovillain offers Rage Powder redirection and Grass/Fire STAB coverage; Lycanroc-Dusk offers fast Tough Claws Rock Slide and Accelerock priority for specific matchup requirements.

decisions.rationale: Feint punishes the strongly telegraphed Protect on opposing Sneasler, allowing Scarf Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum to concentrate enough damage for a likely knockout.
Kingambit safely resists Froslass-Mega’s Blizzard and Shadow Ball, while Dragonite is 4× weak to Ice and risks an immediate knockout.

Mega Evolving Froslass summons Snow, boosting its Defense by 50% and guaranteeing 100% accuracy on Blizzard to threaten an immediate 4x super-effective OHKO onto Choice Scarf Garchomp while dealing spread damage to foe Sneasler. Sneasler uses Protect to safely block opposing Fake Out and fast Ground attacks from Garchomp.
Send in Basculegion alongside Mega Froslass to establish dual-Ghost field presence, completely blanking opposing Sneasler's Close Combat and Feint/Fake Out while securing faster offensive pressure.
Double-target Froslass-Mega; Kowtow Cleave punishes Blizzard or Aurora Veil, while Dire Claw adds chip and a possible status before Sneasler is removed.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Aurora Veil (your side, including ally Basculegion)
decisions.rationale: Setting up Aurora Veil with Froslass negates any Sucker Punch directed at it while drastically reducing incoming damage for both active Pokémon and the benched Kingambit. Basculegion's Aqua Jet moves before Sneasler and faster than Kingambit's Sucker Punch, neutralizing Sucker Punch directed at Basculegion and providing a strong roll to eliminate Sneasler immediately.

Sucker Punch guarantees the Froslass knockout if it attacks, preventing Blizzard. Mega Dragonite then outspeeds Basculegion and pressures it with Dragon Pulse; if Froslass Protects, Dragonite still makes progress into Basculegion.

Froslass is at 30% HP and threatens a 4x Blizzard into Dragonite, making it the prime target for an opposing Kingambit Sucker Punch; Protect blocks this cleanly and preserves Froslass under Aurora Veil. Basculegion uses Adaptability Wave Crash into Kingambit to deal 55.1-93.7%, putting it into Aqua Jet KO range for the following turn while taking minimal spread damage behind Veil.
Sucker Punch removes attacking Froslass before Blizzard, while Dragon Pulse reliably finishes Basculegion. If Froslass Protects, Dragon Pulse still secures Basculegion.
Switch Froslass to Kingambit to blank opposing Sucker Punch and preserve Froslass for endgame cleanup, while Basculegion uses Protect to safely block attacks under Aurora Veil.
Sucker Punch guarantees the Basculegion KO if it attacks, while Heat Wave pressures both foes and substantially damages Kingambit through Aurora Veil.

Coordinated priority attacks (Basculegion's Adaptability Aqua Jet + Kingambit's Sucker Punch) onto the opposing Kingambit guarantee or near-guarantee a knockout before it can execute a 0-priority Low Kick into our Kingambit, preventing any double-target KO threat and securing an endgame advantage against Mega Dragonite.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Heat Wave guarantees the Froslass knockout if Dragonite survives Blizzard while also dealing the most damage to Kingambit.

Sucker Punch priority breaks Dragonite-Mega's Multiscale before it can use Heat Wave/Dragon Pulse, allowing 100%-accurate Snow Blizzard from faster Mega Froslass to guarantee the knockout and win Game 1.

reflections.summary: The loss came from the opening trade: Feint plus Stomping Tantrum correctly removed the protecting Sneasler, but Mega Froslass simultaneously KOed Garchomp and left Sneasler in Aqua Jet range, creating an early numbers deficit. Froslass then established Aurora Veil, and the opponent preserved momentum with well-timed Protects that blanked two Sucker Punches and a Dragon Pulse. Their Basculegion and Kingambit priority converted the advantage, leaving Dragonite alone to fall to Kingambit plus a super-effective Blizzard.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the effective Feint read and respect the opponent’s defensive sequencing, but do not lead Garchomp into the demonstrated Mega Froslass snow mode. Favor a sturdier Kingambit-centered opening and consider bringing Basculegion or Floette over Garchomp so Blizzard cannot generate the same immediate trade. Pressure Froslass before Aurora Veil while avoiding unnecessary Sucker Punch commitments when Protect or a status move is available; preserve enough board presence to prevent Kingambit and Froslass from closing together.
reflections.notebook: Opponent demonstrated a Mega Froslass plus Sneasler lead: Sneasler may Protect turn one while Froslass immediately sets snow and attacks with Blizzard. After losing Sneasler, opponent used Basculegion to pick off a weakened target with Aqua Jet while Froslass established Aurora Veil. Opponent readily cycles Protect and switches Froslass out for Kingambit, then restores snow by returning Froslass later; avoid speculative Sucker Punches and attacks into strongly telegraphed Protects. Next game, avoid leading Garchomp into Mega Froslass, favor a sturdier Kingambit-centered opening, pressure Froslass before Veil, and consider Basculegion or Floette to maintain board presence against the snow mode.

reflections.summary: Mega Froslass's Snow Warning and Blizzard immediately dismantled the opponent's Scarf Garchomp and Feint Sneasler opening, allowing Basculegion and Kingambit to clean up with priority under Aurora Veil against Mega Dragonite and Kingambit.
reflections.adjustment: Anticipate the opponent dropping the Scarf Garchomp lead and potentially bringing Floette-Eternal or Basculegion to challenge our Ice/Ghost pressure; retain Mega Froslass and Kingambit as core pieces while preparing for alternate leads.

decisions.notebook:
Opponent Roster & Confirmed Sets:
- Garchomp: Choice Scarf (Adamant), Stomping Tantrum / Earthquake / Dragon Claw / Rock Slide. Led aggressively turn 1.
- Sneasler: Focus Sash, Poison Touch (Jolly), Feint / Fake Out / Close Combat / Dire Claw. Used Feint turn 1 to break Protect.

- Basculegion: Life Orb, Adaptability (Adamant), Wave Crash / Last Respects / Aqua Jet / Protect (benched G1).

Matchup Notes:
- Mega Froslass outspeeds their unboosted roster (189 Speed) and heavily threatens Garchomp and Mega Dragonite with 100% accurate Blizzard.
- Kingambit with Defiant and Chople-less Sucker Punch/Kowtow Cleave trades effectively into opposing Kingambit and Floette.
- Basculegion Aqua Jet provides reliable cleanup alongside Froslass Blizzard and Kingambit Sucker Punch.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out stops opposing Sneasler from threatening Kingambit unless it Protects, while Kowtow Cleave strongly pressures Froslass and punishes the previously demonstrated Protect-plus-Blizzard line.

Double Protect neutralizes opponent's Jolly Sneasler Fake Out without taking damage or flinching, while Mega Evolving Froslass safely establishes Snow Warning for 100% Blizzard accuracy and +50% Defense.

Switching Basculegion into the likely Close Combat preserves Kingambit via immunity while resisting Blizzard; Dire Claw pressures Froslass without defensive drops and may inflict status before Basculegion threatens it.

Froslass uses 100% accurate Blizzard in snow to deal spread damage to both foes and break foe Sneasler's Focus Sash. Sneasler uses Close Combat into Kingambit, combining with Blizzard to guarantee a KO through Chople Berry while triggering White Herb and Unburden.

Preserve both weakened attackers while exploiting the likely Shadow Ball into Basculegion and reliable Close Combat into Sneasler; Kingambit absorbs Ghost damage and Floette resists Fighting as poison continues wearing down Froslass.

Mega Froslass outspeeds foe Basculegion and heavily threatens to KO it from 74% HP with STAB Shadow Ball before it can move (surviving Aqua Jet if used). Sneasler uses Close Combat into foe Sneasler to secure the KO on the sash-broken target while consuming White Herb to activate Unburden.
Mega Protect preserves Floette from Sneasler, while Sucker Punch pressures an attacking Froslass before Kingambit can be hit by Close Combat.
Bring Basculegion for its Blizzard resistance, Close Combat immunity, and immediate priority pressure while preserving Sneasler’s Fake Out utility for later.

Froslass uses Protect to safely absorb Kingambit's Sucker Punch or any targeting attacks while preserving Snowscape and its HP. Sneasler (344 Speed under Unburden) uses 100% accurate Close Combat into Kingambit, who lacks Protect, dealing 76.3-131.4% through Chople Berry to either KO or bring it to critical HP before it can move.
Protect Basculegion from the guaranteed Shadow Ball KO while Moonblast guarantees the KO on Froslass-Mega if Floette survives Sneasler's inaccurate Gunk Shot.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler with Unburden speed (344) outspeeds Floette-Mega and guarantees a KO with Gunk Shot (107-201%). Froslass-Mega (189 Speed) naturally outspeeds both Floette and Basculegion, and is guaranteed to survive an Aqua Jet from 42% HP (max 40.9%), allowing it to fire a super-effective Shadow Ball (56-105%) into the 74% Basculegion to heavily damage or eliminate it.

Fake Out stops the faster opposing Sneasler while Aqua Jet gives Basculegion its only chance to remove Froslass before Shadow Ball; if Froslass Protects, poison puts it into guaranteed Aqua Jet range next turn.

With Unburden active, Sneasler (Speed 344) outspeeds the entire opposing side and Close Combat guarantees a KO on foe Sneasler from 40% HP. Froslass-Mega (Speed 189) outspeeds Basculegion and hits it with super-effective 100%-accurate Shadow Ball to either KO or bring it into trivial cleanup range for our full-health backline of Kingambit and Basculegion.

Bring in Basculegion to replace fainted Froslass. Basculegion outspeeds foe Basculegion, is immune to foe Sneasler's Close Combat, Fake Out, and Feint, and provides an immediate winning endgame alongside Unburden Sneasler.
No rationale supplied.

Our Basculegion outspeeds the opposing Adamant Basculegion (143 vs 98-130 max) and guarantees an OHKO on it with Last Respects (121.6-229.2%). Our Unburden Sneasler (344 Speed) outspeeds opposing Jolly Sneasler and targets it with 100% accurate Close Combat (32.1-64.5% vs 40% HP) to immediately secure the match win.

reflections.summary: The opponent converted the midgame into consecutive knockouts on Kingambit and Mega Floette, then its faster Basculegion closed turn 7 with Last Respects. You removed Mega Froslass but lost all four Pokémon, ending the semifinal and series 0-2.
reflections.notebook: Opponent demonstrated a Mega Froslass plus Sneasler lead: Sneasler may Protect turn one while Froslass immediately sets snow and attacks with Blizzard. After losing Sneasler, opponent used Basculegion to pick off a weakened target with Aqua Jet while Froslass established Aurora Veil. Opponent readily cycles Protect and switches Froslass out for Kingambit, then restores snow by returning Froslass later; avoid speculative Sucker Punches and attacks into strongly telegraphed Protects. Next game, avoid leading Garchomp into Mega Froslass, favor a sturdier Kingambit-centered opening, pressure Froslass before Veil, and consider Basculegion or Floette to maintain board presence against the snow mode.

retrospective.didWell: Turn 2 was sharp: switching Kingambit to Basculegion caught Close Combat with an immunity while Dire Claw poisoned Mega Froslass. Your turn 3 double switch directed both opposing attacks into resistances and consumed Sneasler’s White Herb. On turn 6, Fake Out plus Aqua Jet cleanly removed Mega Froslass while preventing Sneasler from acting.
retrospective.didPoorly: The turn 4-5 sequence produced no direct damage while Kingambit and Mega Floette were knocked out consecutively. Your selected four lacked speed control, leaving Adamant Basculegion vulnerable to the opposing Jolly Basculegion in the decisive endgame. Feint covered Protect on turn 7, but the opponent attacked, so it provided only chip before both of your remaining Pokémon fainted.
retrospective.wouldChange: At team preview, I would bring Choice Scarf Garchomp over Kingambit to add immediate speed and Rock Slide pressure against the Froslass lead. On turn 4, I would switch Kingambit to Basculegion, reusing its confirmed Close Combat immunity while Floette protected instead of risking Sucker Punch into Froslass. On turn 7, I would double-target the opposing Sneasler with Close Combat and Aqua Jet to maximize the chance of removing it before it moved, rather than pair Feint with a Last Respects that the slower Basculegion never executed.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 by seizing early board control with Mega Froslass and Sneasler. Double Protect on turn 1 safely neutralized opposing Fake Out pressure, and consuming White Herb via Close Combat activated Sneasler's Unburden, allowing it to outspeed and dismantle opposing offensive threats before Basculegion cleanly sealed the match with Last Respects.
reflections.adjustment: Maintain the strong offensive pairing of Mega Froslass and Sneasler for early-game pressure and speed control, while utilizing Sneasler's White Herb Unburden activation and Basculegion's late-game Last Respects cleaning potential.
reflections.notebook:
Team Synergies & Execution Lessons:
- Mega Froslass (189 Speed, Snow Warning): Provides immediate high-speed offensive pressure with 100% accurate Blizzard spread damage and Aurora Veil mitigation option, outpacing the majority of unboosted meta threats.
- Sneasler (White Herb, Unburden): Acts as a potent offensive pivot and cleaner. Consuming White Herb via Close Combat triggers Unburden, granting double Speed to outpace virtually all non-priority attackers and apply massive physical Fighting/Poison pressure.
- Basculegion (Life Orb, Adaptability): Elite late-game anchor. Last Respects gains immense power as allies faint, while Adaptability Aqua Jet secures vital priority knockouts against weakened targets.
- Kingambit (Black Glasses, Defiant): Deterrent against stat-lowering moves and Intimidate, threatening opposing teams with Swords Dance setup and Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave.
- Lycanroc-Dusk & Scovillain: Provide situational flex options with Focus Sash-backed Rock Slide / Accelerock pressure or Rage Powder redirection support depending on matchup needs.

events.text: Aurora Veil up on P1's side
Aurora Veil ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Mirror: lead Froslass+Sneasler to contest Veil and Fake Out sash/Rage Powder. Lycanroc and Basculegion in back. Kingambit stays home vs dual Fighting; Scovillain stays home vs Rock/Poison.
decisions.notebook: Near-mirror. Diffs: my Dire Claw vs their Gunk Shot; my Bascu Adamant vs their Jolly; my Spe Froslass 178, Sneasler 172, Lycanroc 162, Kingambit 70, Scovillain 95. Chart: Ice not SE Fighting; Fighting SE Ice; Water not SE Ice/Steel; Steel not resist Ghost; Dark resists Ghost 0.5x (not immune); FO/Fighting immune on both Ghosts. Nothing here is SE vs Sneasler. No Tailwind/Encore/EQ/TR/Intimidate/Veil-break. FO +3 beats Rage Powder. Mega Froslass (Snow+Veil) over Scovillain. Game1 four: Froslass, Sneasler, Lycanroc, Basculegion. Do not lead Sneasler into double Ghost. Accelerock Froslass/Scovillain; Shadow Ball Ghosts; Sneasler CC Kingambit then Unburden. If they show Kingambit-core or Last Respects unchecked, bring Kingambit game 2. If they show Scovillain, keep Lycanroc.

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Froslass + Basculegion to blank opposing Sneasler's Fake Out and Close Combat options while capitalizing on our Jolly Basculegion outspeeding the opponent's Adamant Basculegion. Sneasler and Kingambit provide powerful late-game cleanup in the back.
decisions.notebook:
Mirror match plan:
- Lead Mega Froslass + Basculegion: Dual Ghost typing completely invalidates opposing Sneasler's Fake Out and Close Combat turn 1.
- Speed Advantage: Our Basculegion is Jolly (143 Speed), strictly outspeeding opponent's Adamant Basculegion (max 130 Speed).
- Backline: Sneasler (White Herb Unburden Fighting/Poison offensive cleaner) + Kingambit (Sucker Punch priority / Kowtow Cleave late-game anchor).

decisions.rationale: Wave Crash OHKOes Froslass; Protect+Mega keeps the setter and sets Snow so Veil can go up next turn. Sneasler is walled, so switch it to Bascu which resists Wave Crash.

Basculegion uses Protect to scout and absorb any Shadow Ball targeted at it, while Froslass Mega Evolves and targets opposing Froslass with Shadow Ball for an immediate OHKO threat. Opposing Sneasler's Fake Out and Close Combat are blocked by Ghost-type immunities.

selection: Aurora Veil (your side, including ally Basculegion)
decisions.rationale: Max-speed Veil first so their Shadow Balls no longer OHKO; Wave Crash still KOs Froslass if they attack, or deals ~66-78% through their Veil.

Send Sneasler for Fake Out on their replacement; Bascu Last Respects their Bascu (mutual KO range, speed uncertain). Sneasler walls nothing from Bascu but disrupts the unknown and threatens Kingambit/Scovillain.

Foe Froslass cannot safely Protect after using it on turn 1. Our Froslass (189 Speed) and Jolly Basculegion (143 Speed) combine Shadow Ball (61.0% min) and Last Respects (46.9% min) into foe Froslass for a guaranteed 107.9% minimum KO without recoil. If our Froslass faints to a speed-tie Shadow Ball, Last Respects scales to 100 BP to guarantee the OHKO regardless, while our 143 Speed strictly outspeeds opponent's Adamant Basculegion (max 130).
Send in Sneasler to establish offensive and Fake Out pressure alongside Basculegion, which outspeeds opposing Basculegion and threatens a guaranteed KO with Last Respects.
Fake Out their Sneasler (only valid FO target) to deny Unburden CC/Gunk, Protect Bascu because Adaptability LR is a guaranteed KO on 64% even through Veil and Bascu Spe is a coin flip vs Jolly.

Our Sneasler uses Fake Out into foe Sneasler to disrupt it (foe Sneasler cannot Fake Out our Ghost-type Basculegion). Our Jolly Basculegion (143 Speed) naturally outspeeds foe Adamant Basculegion (max 130 Speed) and secures a guaranteed KO with Last Respects (81-153% through Aurora Veil vs 63% HP), surviving any incoming Aqua Jet easily.

Jolly Bascu likely outspeeds 119 and Last Respects OHKOs mine through Veil, so attacking loses Bascu for free; consecutive Protect is 1/3. Switch to sash Lycanroc lives Last Respects (41-99% through Veil, sash intact). Sneasler Protect covers the Wave Crash that OHKOs it.

If Last Respects unchecked or they show Kingambit-core, bring Kingambit game 2. If they show Scovillain, keep Lycanroc.

Sneasler using Close Combat into foe Sneasler deals solid chip, safely procs White Herb into Unburden (344 Speed), and instantly OHKOs an incoming Kingambit if the opponent switches.

Sneasler cannot reliably Protect; CC their Sneasler for chip and White Herb Unburden if it lives. Lycanroc is KO'd by any hit so Protect keeps two Pokémon. Do not pivot Sneasler into Last Respects (Ghost 2x KO on Basculegion through Veil) or pivot Lycanroc (expected and easily covered).

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler outspeeds Lycanroc-Dusk and KOs it with Close Combat (triggering White Herb Unburden), while Basculegion targets foe Sneasler with Last Respects for 52-103% through Veil, which also cleanly OHKOs opposing Basculegion if they switch it in.

Their Last Respects guaranteed-KOs Bascu through Veil; Sneasler cannot CC Ghost so it KOs 10% Lycanroc. Protect saves Bascu. Accel chips Sneasler (always before CC) so Aqua Jet KOs it next turn. Leaving 64% Bascu vs 2 is better than dying to LR to KO Sneasler and leaving 10% Lycanroc.

Our Jolly Basculegion (143 Speed) naturally outspeeds foe Adamant Basculegion (max 130 Speed) and double-priority from both foes cannot KO our Basculegion (max combined damage 64.5% vs 71% current HP), allowing Last Respects to cleanly KO foe Basculegion through Aurora Veil.

Turn 2 I won same-prio vs their Jolly Bascu so they are Spe ≤119; Last Respects KOs their Bascu before they can Last Respects me. Protect saves 10% Lycanroc from Sneasler (Protect +4 before Sneasler). If they Protect Bascu instead, stall with both alive is still better than losing Bascu.

If they show Scovillain, keep Lycanroc. Their Sneasler still held White Herb after CC into Protect (Unburden never doubled). 4th is Lycanroc/Kingambit/Scovillain.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds and KOs 9% Lycanroc-Dusk with Close Combat. Our Jolly Basculegion (143 Spe) outspeeds opponent's Adamant Basculegion (max 130 Spe) and cleanly OHKOs it with Last Respects. Even if both foes target Basculegion with their respective priority moves (Accelerock + Aqua Jet), their combined maximum damage cannot KO Basculegion from 71% HP.

Fainted slot must pass. CC is the only move that can KO Sneasler; Accel/RS cannot. Spe vs Sneasler is a range so CC is not guaranteed to fire, but it is the sole path to removing a Pokémon before Lycanroc dies.

Lycanroc-Dusk is the opponent's sole remaining Pokémon at 9% HP with its Focus Sash broken. Sneasler's Close Combat (172 Speed) naturally outspeeds Lycanroc-Dusk (max 162 Speed) and Basculegion's Aqua Jet offers priority coverage, guaranteeing the final knockout regardless of opposing move choice.

- Opponent team revealed: Froslass-Mega, Sneasler (White Herb), Basculegion (Adamant Life Orb), Lycanroc-Dusk (Focus Sash, Accelerock/CC/Rock Slide/Protect).

reflections.summary: Lost a near-mirror Last Respects war: their Jolly LO Adaptability Bascu outsped my Adamant 119, farmed KO count after the Mega Froslass trade, and I never damaged it. Leading Sneasler into Froslass+Bascu forced an instant pivot; Lycanroc sash was broken by Respects and could not threaten Bascu. Veil went up the same turn Froslass died.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Kingambit to resist Last Respects and Sucker Punch their Bascu. Do not lead Sneasler into Froslass+Bascu—lead Froslass+Kingambit or Froslass+Bascu. Keep Mega Froslass over Scovillain. Never leave Kingambit in vs their Sneasler CC (4x). 4th still unknown.

Accelerock Froslass/Scovillain; Shadow Ball Ghosts; Sneasler CC Kingambit then Unburden. Their LO Adaptability Last Respects is the win con—bring Kingambit, Sucker Punch Bascu; respect 4x CC on Kingambit. If they show Scovillain, keep Lycanroc. Their Sneasler White Herb unused (CC into Protect, Unburden never doubled). 4th still Lycanroc/Kingambit/Scovillain.

reflections.summary: Won Game 1 by leveraging our Jolly Basculegion's speed advantage (143 Spe vs opponent's Adamant 130 Spe) to dominate the mirror, combined with a strong Mega Froslass + Basculegion lead that pressured early KOs with Last Respects and maintained endgame positioning.
reflections.adjustment: Maintain the Mega Froslass + Basculegion lead with Sneasler and Kingambit/Lycanroc in reserve, continuing to exploit our Jolly Basculegion outspeeding their Basculegion in Last Respects trades while anticipating potential Kingambit counter-leads.
reflections.notebook:
Mirror Match Analysis & Confirmed Specs:
- Opponent Sets:
  * Froslass-Mega: Timid, Blizzard / Shadow Ball / Aurora Veil / Protect (Froslassite)
  * Basculegion: Adamant (max 130 Spe), Adaptability, Wave Crash / Last Respects / Aqua Jet / Protect (Life Orb)
  * Sneasler: Adamant, Unburden, Fake Out / Close Combat / Dire Claw / Protect (White Herb)
  * Lycanroc-Dusk: Adamant, Tough Claws, Accelerock / Close Combat / Rock Slide / Protect (Focus Sash)
  * Kingambit: Adamant, Defiant, Kowtow Cleave / Sucker Punch / Swords Dance / Protect (Black Glasses)
  * Scovillain: Bold, Moody, Overheat / Giga Drain / Rage Powder / Protect (Scovillainite)
- Structural Advantages:
  * Our Jolly Basculegion (143 Spe) strictly outspeeds opponent's Adamant Basculegion (130 Spe), winning any head-to-head Last Respects duel.
  * Dual Ghost lead (Mega Froslass + Basculegion) nullifies opponent's Fake Out and Close Combat options on turn 1.
- Tactical Plan for Game 2:
  * Retain Mega Froslass + Basculegion lead; use Basculegion's Speed tier to threaten OHKOs on their Ghost/Water weak slots.
  * Keep Kingambit and Sneasler ready in the back to handle Lycanroc priority and finish opposing Sneasler/Kingambit.

  * Dual Ghost lead (Mega Froslass + Basculegion) nullifies opponent's Fake Out and Close Combat options on turn 1.
- Tactical Plan for Game 2:
  * Retain Mega Froslass + Basculegion lead; use Basculegion's Speed tier to threaten OHKOs on their Ghost/Water weak slots.
  * Keep Kingambit and Sneasler ready in the back to handle Lycanroc priority and finish opposing Sneasler/Kingambit.

Keep Gambit vs Bascu; respect 4x CC. Kowtow OHKOs their Lass even through Veil. If they show Scov, Lycanroc next game.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve Froslass to establish Snow via Snow Warning and Protect against turn 1 aggression/speed ties, while pivoting Basculegion out to Kingambit, which resists all of the opponent's active offensive STABs (Ghost, Dark, Ice) and invalidates any Sucker Punch.

decisions.rationale: Veil now while Sneasler cannot Fake Out. Kowtow KOs their Lass if they attack/SD and still deals ~74-88% through 2/3 Veil; Sucker Punch would fail into Veil.

selection: Aurora Veil (your side, including ally Kingambit)
decisions.rationale: Using Aurora Veil on Froslass-Mega and Swords Dance on Kingambit blanks any Sucker Punch attempts from the opposing Kingambit since both actions are status moves. Aurora Veil establishes defensive screens for our side under Snowscape, while +2 Kingambit creates an immediate win condition against the opposing team.
Foe +2 Gambit OHKOs Lass through Veil with Kowtow or Sucker; Protect makes Sucker fail and blocks Kowtow. Kowtow still KOs 21% Lass if it attacks, and unlike Sucker it hits a switch-in.

decisions.rationale: Mega Froslass uses Protect to safely absorb the opposing Mega Froslass's anticipated attack without risking a Speed tie. Meanwhile, our +2 Kingambit targets the opposing Mega Froslass with Kowtow Cleave, dealing 97.2-190.3% damage through Aurora Veil for a near-guaranteed KO while retaining full board control.

Lass dies to +2 Sucker/Kowtow if it stays and attacks; consecutive Protect is 1/3. Switch Lass to Sneasler (Kowtow is 0.5x, lives) and Kowtow their 21% Lass (covers Protect-fail and switch-ins; Sucker Punch would whiff a switch).

Send Bascu to pair with Gambit. Last Respects (BP100) threatens KO range on Sneasler/Lycanroc and chips Scov; Wave Crash does ~50% to their Gambit through Veil (Lass does ~20%). Both Ghosts eat +2 Dark OHKO so Protect mindgames are required either way; Bascu is the stronger offensive presence and scales if more faint. Do not forfeit.

Target foe Froslass with Shadow Ball from our Mega Froslass and +2 Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit. Kowtow Cleave has an overwhelming OHKO roll through Aurora Veil (97.2-190.3%) and Shadow Ball guarantees the KO if we win the Speed tie, while Kowtow Cleave punishes any switch-in into slot 1 (OHKOing Basculegion).

Send in Sneasler to pressure foe Kingambit with a guaranteed 4x STAB Close Combat OHKO through Aurora Veil while outspeeding foe Basculegion (172 Spe vs max 130 Spe). Keeping Jolly Basculegion (143 Spe) in reserve secures a clean late-game win with high-power Last Respects against their remaining Ghost-type slots.

Their Sneasler CC OHKOs Kingambit through Veil and +2 Dark OHKOs Bascu through Veil, so the expected line is CC/FO Kingambit plus Kowtow/Sucker Bascu. Switch Kingambit into Ghost-immune Froslass and Protect Bascu: Fighting/Normal do 0, Sucker Punch fails into Protect/switch, and Kowtow Bascu is blocked. Snow Warning also refreshes.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds both opposing Pokémon (172 Spe vs max 130 Basculegion and max 102 Kingambit) and Close Combat achieves a guaranteed OHKO on foe Kingambit even through Aurora Veil (101.9-175.4%). Our +2 Kingambit guarantees an OHKO on foe Basculegion with Kowtow Cleave (118.5-223.6% through Veil). If either foe uses Protect, the other is cleanly removed, keeping us in complete control with an unblemished Basculegion on our bench.

Sneasler is walled (CC/FO immune, Gunk Shot ~20%) so they can KO only one mon via +2 Kingambit. Both of mine outspeed Kingambit, so Kowtow lets both attacks through; they should Kowtow not Sucker because Aqua Jet is on the sheet and would make Sucker fail. Wave Crash the Kingambit that has to attack (40-68% through Veil). Shadow Ball the Sneasler slot: chips if it stays, punishes a Bascu switch-in with SE Ghost.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler uses Protect to preserve its HP to cleanly handle opposing Kingambit later, while our +2 Black Glasses Kingambit uses Kowtow Cleave to guarantee a 1-hit KO on opposing Basculegion through Aurora Veil.

Their lethal is Sneasler CC into Kingambit (guaranteed OHKO) plus +2 Sucker Punch/Kowtow into Lass (guaranteed OHKO). No remaining switches; neither foe is KO'd this turn if they Sucker Punch Lass first. Double Protect is the only joint action that survives that pair.

Our +2 Atk Kingambit's Sucker Punch into Froslass-Mega is a guaranteed priority OHKO (119.8-235.9%), eliminating Froslass before it can attack Sneasler. If either foe Protects, the unprotected target is removed, cleanly securing the match and tournament.
SP+SB both hit Sneasler before CC. Offensive Unburden is ~93-109% combined so Sneasler can faint before CC, saving Kingambit for the 1v2 vs 48% Gambit+Bascu if they Kowtow rather than SP Lass.

Sneasler's Close Combat guarantees an OHKO on foe Kingambit (4x weakness, 152.7-262.9%). Our +2 Black Glasses Kingambit uses priority Sucker Punch into Mega Froslass, which OHKOs before Froslass can act if it attacks. Both opponent slots faced consecutive Protect penalties and are cleaned up.

retrospective.didWell: Mega Evolving Froslass on turn 1 set Snow, and turn 2 Aurora Veil plus Kowtow Cleave dropped their Froslass to 21% before you finished it on turn 4. Switching Kingambit to Froslass-Mega on turn 5 made Close Combat immune while Basculegion’s Protect blocked the +2 Kowtow Cleave. Double Protect on turn 7 correctly made their Sucker Punch fail and stopped Close Combat.
retrospective.didPoorly: Turn 1 Sucker Punch failed against dual Protect and a switch, so your Kingambit never Swords Danced while theirs reached +2 Attack. Hard-switching Sneasler on turn 4 walked it into Shadow Ball and a KO Kowtow Cleave with no attack of its own. Wave Crash only cut Kingambit to 48% before Basculegion fainted, and the turn 8 Sucker Punch into Sneasler left it at 42% even on a critical hit as you lost both Pokémon.
retrospective.wouldChange: On turn 1, Swords Dance or Protect with Kingambit instead of Sucker Punching into Protects and a possible switch. Keep Mega Froslass in on turn 4 to finish the 21% Froslass rather than switching Sneasler into the +2 Kingambit. On turn 8, Sucker Punch their Kingambit or Protect instead of targeting Dark-resistant Sneasler.
